title.zh: 卷32 志第27 經籍一
title.raw: 卷32 志第27 經籍一 Volume 32 Treatises 27: Bibliography 1

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 序夫經籍也者，機神之妙旨，聖哲之能事，所以經天地，緯陰陽，正紀綱，弘道德，顯仁足以利物，藏用足以獨善。

translations.literal: Preface: As for the classics and records, they are the subtle purport of the spirit's workings and the achievement of sages and worthies, by which one spans Heaven and Earth, aligns yin and yang, sets right the fundamental norms, and spreads the Way and virtue; when manifest, benevolence suffices to benefit things; when hidden, usefulness suffices for self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Preface: The classics and records embody the subtle truth of the spirit's workings and the achievement of sages and worthies. Through them one spans Heaven and Earth, aligns yin and yang, sets right the fundamental norms, and spreads the Way and virtue. Revealed, their benevolence suffices to benefit all things; concealed, their usefulness suffices for self-cultivation alone.

sentences.zh: 學之者將殖焉，不學者將落焉。

translations.literal: Those who study them will flourish; those who do not study them will decline.
translations.idiomatic: Those who study them will flourish; those who do not will fall behind.

sentences.zh: 大業崇之，則成欽明之德；

translations.literal: When a great enterprise honors them, it brings forth the virtue of profound discernment;
translations.idiomatic: When a great enterprise honors them, it brings forth the virtue of profound discernment;

sentences.zh: 匹夫克念，則有王公之重。

translations.literal: When an ordinary man holds them in mind, he has the weight of kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When an ordinary man keeps them in mind, he carries the weight of kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 其王者之所以樹風聲，流顯號，美教化，移風俗，何莫由乎斯道。

translations.literal: How can kings establish their reputation, transmit their glorious titles, cultivate fine teachings, and transform customs without this Way?
translations.idiomatic: How can kings establish their reputation, transmit their glorious titles, cultivate fine teachings, and transform customs except through this Way?

sentences.zh: 故曰：其為人也，溫柔敦厚，《詩》教也；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: A person formed by the teaching of the Odes is gentle and sincere;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: A person formed by the teaching of the Odes is gentle and sincere;

sentences.zh: 疏通知遠，《書》教也；

translations.literal: Penetrating in knowledge and far-reaching in vision—this is the teaching of the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: Penetrating in knowledge and far-reaching in vision—this is the teaching of the Documents;

sentences.zh: 廣博易良，《樂》教也；

translations.literal: Broad in spirit and readily good—this is the teaching of Music;
translations.idiomatic: Broad in spirit and readily good—this is the teaching of Music;

sentences.zh: 潔靜精微，《易》教也；

translations.literal: Pure, quiet, subtle, and precise—this is the teaching of the Changes;
translations.idiomatic: Pure, quiet, subtle, and precise—this is the teaching of the Changes;

sentences.zh: 恭儉莊敬，《禮》教也；

translations.literal: Respectful, frugal, dignified, and reverent—this is the teaching of the Rites;
translations.idiomatic: Respectful, frugal, dignified, and reverent—this is the teaching of the Rites;

sentences.zh: 屬辭比事，《春秋》教也。

translations.literal: Skilled in linking words and comparing events—this is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in linking words and comparing events—this is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 遭時制宜，質文迭用，應之以通變，通變之以中庸。

translations.literal: Meeting the needs of the age, substance and ornament alternate in use; one responds with adaptability, and through adaptability one reaches the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the needs of the age, substance and ornament alternate in use; one responds with adaptability, and through adaptability one reaches the mean.

sentences.zh: 中庸則可久，通變則可大。

translations.literal: The mean may endure; adaptability may expand.
translations.idiomatic: The mean may endure; adaptability may expand.

sentences.zh: 其教有適，其用無窮。

translations.literal: Its teaching is appropriate; its uses are inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: Its teaching is appropriate; its uses are inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 實仁義之陶鈞，誠道德之橐籥也。

translations.literal: It is truly the potter's wheel of benevolence and righteousness, the bellows of the Way and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: It is truly the potter's wheel of benevolence and righteousness, the bellows of the Way and virtue.

sentences.zh: 其為用大矣，隨時之義深矣，言無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: Its function is great; the meaning of acting in accord with the times runs deep—words cannot exhaust praise of it.
translations.idiomatic: Its function is great, and the meaning of acting in accord with the times runs deep—words cannot exhaust praise of it.

sentences.zh: 故曰：不疾而速，不行而至。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: Without haste, yet swift; without going, yet arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: Without haste, yet swift; without going, yet arriving.

sentences.zh: 今之所以知古，後之所以知今，其斯之謂也。

translations.literal: That the present should know the past and the future should know the present is what is meant by this.
translations.idiomatic: That the present should know the past and the future should know the present—this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 是以大道方行，俯龜象而設卦；

translations.literal: Thus when the Great Way was first put into practice, Fu Xi looked down at the tortoise and contemplated its markings and fashioned the hexagrams;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Great Way was first put into practice, Fu Xi looked down at the tortoise, contemplated its markings, and fashioned the hexagrams;

sentences.zh: 後聖有作，仰鳥跡以成文。

translations.literal: and when the sage of later times arose, he looked up at the tracks of birds and completed the written script.
translations.idiomatic: and when the sage of later times arose, he looked up at the tracks of birds and completed the written script.

sentences.zh: 書契已傳，繩木棄而不用；

translations.literal: Once written contracts were transmitted, knotted cords were abandoned and no longer used;
translations.idiomatic: Once written contracts were transmitted, knotted cords were abandoned and no longer used;

sentences.zh: 史官既立，經籍於是與焉。

translations.literal: once the historiographers were established, the classics and records came into being along with them.
translations.idiomatic: once the historiographers were established, the classics and records came into being along with them.

sentences.zh: 夫經籍也者，先聖據龍圖，握鳳紀，南面以君天下者，咸有史官，以紀言行。

translations.literal: As for the classics and records, the earlier sages, having received the Dragon Chart and grasped the Phoenix Register, and facing south to rule All-under-Heaven, all had historiographers to record words and deeds.
translations.idiomatic: As for the classics and records, the earlier sages who received the Dragon Chart and grasped the Phoenix Register, and faced south to rule All-under-Heaven, all had historiographers to record words and deeds.

sentences.zh: 言則左史書之，動則右史書之。

translations.literal: When the ruler spoke, the left historiographer recorded it; when he acted, the right historiographer recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler spoke, the left historiographer recorded it; when he acted, the right historiographer recorded it.

sentences.zh: 故曰「君舉必書」，懲勸斯在。

translations.literal: Hence the saying "the ruler's every act must be written down"—in this lay censure and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying "the ruler's every act must be written down"—in this lay censure and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 考之前載，則《三墳》、《五典》、《八索》、《九丘》之類是也。

translations.literal: Looking to earlier records, works such as the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds belong to this.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to earlier records, works such as the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds belong to this category.

sentences.zh: 下逮殷、周，史官尤備，紀言書事，靡有闕遺，則《周禮》所稱，太史掌建邦之六典、八法、八則，以詔王治；

translations.literal: Down through Yin and Zhou, the historiographers were especially complete, recording words and events without omission. Thus what the Rites of Zhou describes: the Grand Historiographer was charged with establishing the six canons, eight laws, and eight regulations of the state, to instruct the king in governance;
translations.idiomatic: Down through Yin and Zhou, the historiographers were especially complete, recording words and events without omission. Thus what the Rites of Zhou describes: the Grand Historiographer was charged with establishing the six canons, eight laws, and eight regulations of the state, to instruct the king in governance;

sentences.zh: 小史掌邦國之志，定世系，辨昭穆；

translations.literal: the Minor Historiographer was charged with keeping the records of the states, fixing genealogies, and distinguishing senior and junior lines of descent;
translations.idiomatic: the Minor Historiographer was charged with keeping the records of the states, fixing genealogies, and distinguishing senior and junior lines of descent;

sentences.zh: 內史掌王之八柄，策命而貳之；

translations.literal: the Inner Historiographer was charged with the king's eight powers of command, issuing edicts and keeping duplicate copies;
translations.idiomatic: the Inner Historiographer was charged with the king's eight powers of command, issuing edicts and keeping duplicate copies;

sentences.zh: 外史掌王之外令及四方之志，三皇、五帝之書；

translations.literal: the Outer Historiographer was charged with the king's external commands and the records of the four quarters, as well as books of the Three Emperors and Five Thearchs;
translations.idiomatic: the Outer Historiographer was charged with the king's external commands and the records of the four quarters, as well as books of the Three Emperors and Five Thearchs;

sentences.zh: 禦史掌邦國都鄙萬民之治令，以贊塚宰。

translations.literal: the Supervising Historiographer was charged with the governing orders for the states, capitals, districts, and myriad people, to assist the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: the Supervising Historiographer was charged with the governing orders for the states, capitals, districts, and myriad people, to assist the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 此則天子之史，凡有五焉。

translations.literal: These were the historiographers at the Son of Heaven's court—five in all.
translations.idiomatic: These were the historiographers at the Son of Heaven's court—five in all.

sentences.zh: 諸侯亦各有國史，分掌其職。

translations.literal: Each feudal lord likewise had his own state historiographers, each fulfilling his office.
translations.idiomatic: Each feudal lord likewise had his own state historiographers, each fulfilling his office.

sentences.zh: 則《春秋傳》，晉趙穿弑靈公，太史董狐書曰「趙盾殺其君」，以示於朝。

translations.literal: Thus in the Zuo Commentary, when Zhao Chuan of Jin assassinated Duke Ling, Grand Historiographer Dong Hu wrote, "Zhao Dun killed his lord," and displayed it in court.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Zuo Commentary, when Zhao Chuan of Jin assassinated Duke Ling, Grand Historiographer Dong Hu wrote, "Zhao Dun killed his lord," and displayed it in court.

sentences.zh: 宣子曰「不然。

translations.literal: Xuanshi said, "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshi said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「子為正卿，亡不越境，反不討賊，非子而誰？

translations.literal: " He replied, "You were chief minister; you fled but did not cross the border, and upon your return you did not punish the villain—if not you, then who?"
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "You were chief minister; you fled but did not cross the border, and upon your return you did not punish the villain—if not you, then who?"

sentences.zh: 」齊崔杼弑莊公，太史書曰「崔杼弑其君」，崔子殺之。

translations.literal: In Qi, Cui Zhu assassinated Duke Zhuang; the Grand Historiographer wrote, "Cui Zhu assassinated his lord," and Cui had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, Cui Zhu assassinated Duke Zhuang; the Grand Historiographer wrote, "Cui Zhu assassinated his lord," and Cui had him killed.

sentences.zh: 其弟嗣書，死者二人。

translations.literal: His younger brother succeeded to the post and wrote the same; two men died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother succeeded to the post and wrote the same; two men died.

sentences.zh: 其弟又書，乃舍之。

translations.literal: Another younger brother wrote again, and Cui then let the matter go.
translations.idiomatic: Another younger brother wrote again, and Cui then let the matter go.

sentences.zh: 南史聞太史盡死，執簡以往，聞既書矣，乃還。

translations.literal: The Southern Historiographer, hearing that the Grand Historiographers had all been killed, took up his bamboo slips and set out, but hearing that it had already been written, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Historiographer, hearing that the Grand Historiographers had all been killed, took up his bamboo slips and set out, but hearing that it had already been written, he returned.

sentences.zh: 楚靈王與右尹子革語，左史倚相趨而過。

translations.literal: King Ling of Chu was conversing with Right Intendant Zige when Left Historiographer Yi Xiang hurried past.
translations.idiomatic: King Ling of Chu was conversing with Right Intendant Zige when Left Historiographer Yi Xiang hurried past.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「此良史也，能讀《三墳》、《五典》、《八索》、《九丘》。

translations.literal: The king said, "This is a fine historiographer; he can read the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "This is a fine historiographer; he can read the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds."

sentences.zh: 」然則諸侯史官，亦非一人而已，皆以記言書事，太史總而裁之，以成國家之典。

translations.literal: Thus the historiographers of the feudal lords were not a single person each; all recorded words and events, and the Grand Historiographer gathered and adjudicated them to form the canonical records of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the historiographers of the feudal lords were not a single person each; all recorded words and events, and the Grand Historiographer gathered and adjudicated them to form the canonical records of the state.

sentences.zh: 不虛美，不隱惡，故得有所懲勸，遺文可觀，則《左傳》稱《周志》，《國語》有《鄭書》之類是也。

translations.literal: They did not embellish with false praise, nor conceal evil; thus censure and encouragement could take effect, and surviving texts remain worth reading—such as when the Zuo Commentary cites the Records of Zhou, and the Discourses of the States contains the Records of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: They did not embellish with false praise, nor conceal evil; thus censure and encouragement could take effect, and surviving texts remain worth reading—such as when the Zuo Commentary cites the Records of Zhou, and the Discourses of the States contains the Records of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 暨夫周室道衰，紀綱散亂，國異政，家殊俗，褒貶失實，隳紊舊章。

translations.literal: When the Zhou royal house's Way declined, its fundamental norms fell into disorder, states differed in policy and families differed in custom, praise and blame lost their truth, and old regulations were overturned and confused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou royal house's Way declined, its fundamental norms fell into disorder, states differed in policy and families differed in custom, praise and blame lost their truth, and old regulations were overturned and confused.

sentences.zh: 孔丘以大聖之才，當傾頹之運，歎鳳鳥之不至，惜將墜於斯文，乃述《易》道而刪《詩》、《書》，修《春秋》而正《雅》、《頌》。

translations.literal: Confucius, with the talent of a great sage, in an age of collapse, lamented that the phoenix had not come and feared that this culture was about to fall, and so expounded the Way of the Changes, edited the Odes and Documents, revised the Spring and Autumn, and corrected the Major and Minor Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, with the talent of a great sage, in an age of collapse, lamented that the phoenix had not come and feared that this culture was about to fall. He expounded the Way of the Changes, edited the Odes and Documents, revised the Spring and Autumn, and corrected the Major and Minor Odes.

sentences.zh: 壞禮崩樂，鹹得其所。

translations.literal: Where rites were broken and music collapsed, all were restored to their proper places.
translations.idiomatic: Where rites were broken and music collapsed, all were restored to their proper places.

sentences.zh: 自哲人萎而微言絕，七十子散而大義乖，戰國縱橫，真偽莫辨，諸子之言，紛然淆亂。

translations.literal: From the time the wise man withered away and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples scattered and the great meaning went astray; in the Warring States era the vertical and horizontal alliances flourished, truth and falsehood could not be distinguished, and the words of the various masters became confused and jumbled.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the wise man withered away and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples scattered and the great meaning went astray. In the Warring States era the vertical and horizontal alliances flourished, truth and falsehood could not be distinguished, and the words of the various masters became confused and jumbled.

sentences.zh: 聖人之至德喪矣，先王之要道亡矣。

translations.literal: The utmost virtue of the sage was lost; the essential Way of the earlier kings perished.
translations.idiomatic: The utmost virtue of the sage was lost; the essential Way of the earlier kings perished.

sentences.zh: 陵夷踳駁，以至於秦。

translations.literal: Decline, confusion, and contradiction continued until the Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Decline, confusion, and contradiction continued until the Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦政奮豺狼之心，剗先代之跡，焚《詩》、《書》，坑儒士，以刀筆吏為師，制挾書之令。

translations.literal: The Qin government roused the heart of wolf and jackal, erased the traces of earlier generations, burned the Odes and Documents, buried the scholars alive, made scribes its teachers, and issued the law against keeping books.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin government roused the heart of wolf and jackal, erased the traces of earlier generations, burned the Odes and Documents, buried the scholars alive, made scribes its teachers, and issued the law against keeping books.

sentences.zh: 學者逃難，竄伏山林，或失本經，口以傳說。

translations.literal: Scholars fled in hardship, hiding in mountains and forests, or lost the original classics and passed them on by word of mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars fled in hardship, hiding in mountains and forests, or lost the original classics and passed them on by word of mouth.

sentences.zh: 漢氏誅除秦、項，未及下車，先命叔孫通草綿蕝之儀，救擊柱之弊。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty destroyed Qin and Xiang Yu, and before even stepping down from the chariot, first ordered Shu Sun Tong to draft the rites of the cotton-mat altar, to remedy the evil of striking the pillar.
translations.idiomatic: The Han dynasty destroyed Qin and Xiang Yu, and before even stepping down from the chariot, first ordered Shu Sun Tong to draft the rites of the cotton-mat altar, to remedy the evil of striking the pillar.

sentences.zh: 其後張蒼治律曆，陸賈撰《新語》，曹參薦蓋公言黃老，惠帝除挾書之律，儒者始以其業行於民間。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhang Cang regulated the calendar, Lu Jia composed the New Discourses, Cao Shen recommended Lord Gai's teachings on Yellow Emperor and Laozi, Emperor Hui abolished the law against keeping books, and Confucian scholars at last practiced their craft among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Zhang Cang regulated the calendar, Lu Jia composed the New Discourses, Cao Shen recommended Lord Gai's teachings on the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, Emperor Hui abolished the law against keeping books, and Confucian scholars at last practiced their craft among the people.

sentences.zh: 猶以去聖既遠，經籍散逸，簡劄錯亂，傳說紕繆，遂使《書》分為二，《詩》分為三，《論語》有齊、魯之殊，《春秋》有數家之傳。

translations.literal: Yet because the sage was already far removed, the classics and records were scattered and lost, bamboo slips were confused, and transmitted accounts were erroneous, so that the Documents came to be divided into two versions, the Odes into three, the Analects had Qi and Lu variants, and the Spring and Autumn had several schools of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the sage was already far removed, the classics and records were scattered and lost, bamboo slips were confused, and transmitted accounts were erroneous, so that the Documents came to be divided into two versions, the Odes into three, the Analects had Qi and Lu variants, and the Spring and Autumn had several schools of transmission.

sentences.zh: 其餘互有踳駁，不可勝言。

translations.literal: The rest contradicted one another in ways too numerous to recount.
translations.idiomatic: The rest contradicted one another in ways too numerous to recount.

sentences.zh: 此其所以博而寡要，勞而少功者也。

translations.literal: This is why their learning was broad yet lacked essentials, laborious yet yielded little result.
translations.idiomatic: This is why their learning was broad yet lacked essentials, laborious yet yielded little result.

sentences.zh: 武帝置太史公，命天下計書，先上太史，副上丞相，開獻書之路，置寫書之官，外有太常、太史、博士之藏，內有延閣、廣內、秘室之府。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu established the Grand Historiographer, ordered that reports from throughout the realm be sent first to the Grand Historiographer and a copy to the Chancellor, opened the path for presenting books, established offices for copying books, and had external repositories in the Grand Sacrificer, Grand Historiographer, and Erudite, and internal repositories in the Extended Pavilion, Broad Inner Hall, and Secret Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu established the Grand Historiographer, ordered that reports from throughout the realm be sent first to the Grand Historiographer and a copy to the Chancellor, opened the path for presenting books, established offices for copying books, and had external repositories in the Grand Sacrificer, Grand Historiographer, and Erudite, and internal repositories in the Extended Pavilion, Broad Inner Hall, and Secret Chamber.

sentences.zh: 司馬談父子世居太史，探采前代，斷自軒皇，逮于孝武，作《史記》一百三十篇。

translations.literal: Sima Tan and his son, for generations holding the post of Grand Historiographer, gathered materials from earlier ages, beginning from the Yellow Emperor down to Emperor Wu, and composed the Records in one hundred thirty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tan and his son, for generations holding the post of Grand Historiographer, gathered materials from earlier ages, beginning from the Yellow Emperor down to Emperor Wu, and composed the Records in one hundred thirty chapters.

sentences.zh: 詳其禮制，蓋史官之舊也。

translations.literal: Examining its ritual system, it was largely the old practice of the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Examining its ritual system, it was largely the old practice of the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 至於孝成，秘藏之書，頗有亡散，乃使謁者陳農，求遺書於天下。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Cheng, many books in the secret repository had been lost and scattered, so he sent Attendant Chen Nong to seek lost books throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Cheng, many books in the secret repository had been lost and scattered, so he sent Attendant Chen Nong to seek lost books throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 命光祿大夫劉向校經傳諸子詩賦，步兵校尉任宏校兵書，太史令尹咸校數術，太醫監李柱國校方技。

translations.literal: He ordered Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Xiang to collate the classics, commentaries, various masters, odes, and rhapsodies; Commandant of Footsoldiers Ren Hong to collate military books; Grand Historiographer Yin Xian to collate numerology; and Director of the Imperial Physicians Li Zhuguo to collate technical arts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Xiang to collate the classics, commentaries, various masters, odes, and rhapsodies; Commandant of Footsoldiers Ren Hong to collate military books; Grand Historiographer Yin Xian to collate numerology; and Director of the Imperial Physicians Li Zhuguo to collate technical arts.

sentences.zh: 每一書就，向輒撰為一錄，論其指歸，辨其訛謬，敘而奏之。

translations.literal: Whenever a book was finished, Xiang would compose a record for it, discussing its purport, distinguishing its errors, arranging it, and submitting it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a book was finished, Xiang would compose a record for it, discussing its purport, distinguishing its errors, arranging it, and submitting it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 向卒後，哀帝使其子歆嗣父之業。

translations.literal: After Xiang died, Emperor Ai had his son Xin succeed to his father's work.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang died, Emperor Ai had his son Xin succeed to his father's work.

sentences.zh: 乃徙溫室中書於天祿閣上。

translations.literal: He then moved the palace library books from the Green Chamber to the upper level of the Hall of Heavenly Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved the palace library books from the Green Chamber to the upper level of the Hall of Heavenly Blessings.

sentences.zh: 歆遂總括群篇，撮其指要，著為《七略》：一曰《集略》，二曰《六藝略》，三曰《諸子略》，四曰《詩賦略》，五曰《兵書略》，六曰《術數略》，七曰《方技略》。

translations.literal: Xin then gathered all the texts together, extracted their essentials, and compiled the Seven Summaries: first, the General Summary; second, the Summary of the Six Arts; third, the Summary of the Various Masters; fourth, the Summary of Odes and Rhapsodies; fifth, the Summary of Military Books; sixth, the Summary of Numerology; seventh, the Summary of Technical Arts.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then gathered all the texts together, extracted their essentials, and compiled the Seven Summaries: first, the General Summary; second, the Summary of the Six Arts; third, the Summary of the Various Masters; fourth, the Summary of Odes and Rhapsodies; fifth, the Summary of Military Books; sixth, the Summary of Numerology; seventh, the Summary of Technical Arts.

sentences.zh: 大凡三萬三千九十卷。

translations.literal: In all, thirty-three thousand ninety scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all, thirty-three thousand ninety scrolls.

sentences.zh: 王莽之末，又被焚燒。

translations.literal: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, they were burned again.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, they were burned again.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，篤好文雅，明、章繼軌，尤重經術。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he deeply loved refined culture, and Emperors Ming and Zhang followed his course, especially honoring classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he deeply loved refined culture, and Emperors Ming and Zhang followed his course, especially honoring classical learning.

sentences.zh: 四方鴻生巨儒，負袠自遠而至者，不可勝算。

translations.literal: Great scholars from the four quarters, bearing their bundles and coming from afar, were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Great scholars from the four quarters, bearing their bundles and coming from afar, were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 石室、蘭台，彌以充積。

translations.literal: The Stone Chamber and Orchid Terrace became ever more filled.
translations.idiomatic: The Stone Chamber and Orchid Terrace became ever more filled.

sentences.zh: 又于東觀及仁壽閣集新書，校書郎班固、傅毅等典掌焉。

translations.literal: They also gathered new books at the Eastern Pavilion and the Hall of Benevolent Longevity, with Collators Ban Gu, Fu Yi, and others in charge.
translations.idiomatic: They also gathered new books at the Eastern Pavilion and the Hall of Benevolent Longevity, with Collators Ban Gu, Fu Yi, and others in charge.

sentences.zh: 並依《七略》而為書部，固又編之，以為《漢書·藝文志》。

translations.literal: They all followed the Seven Summaries in arranging book categories, and Gu further compiled them into the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: They all followed the Seven Summaries in arranging book categories, and Gu further compiled them into the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 董卓之亂，獻帝西遷，圖書縑帛，軍人皆取為帷囊。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, when Emperor Xian moved west, the books and silk scrolls were all taken by soldiers for curtains and bags.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, when Emperor Xian moved west, the books and silk scrolls were all taken by soldiers for curtains and bags.

sentences.zh: 所收而西，猶七十餘載。

translations.literal: What was collected and taken west still amounted to more than seventy cartloads.
translations.idiomatic: What was collected and taken west still amounted to more than seventy cartloads.

sentences.zh: 兩京大亂，掃地皆盡。

translations.literal: In the great chaos of the two capitals, everything was swept away and lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the great chaos of the two capitals, everything was swept away and lost.

sentences.zh: 魏氏代漢，采掇遺亡，藏在秘書中、外三閣。

translations.literal: When the Wei replaced the Han, they gathered what had been lost and stored it in the inner and outer three pavilions of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei replaced the Han, they gathered what had been lost and stored it in the inner and outer three pavilions of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏秘書郎鄭默，始制《中經》，秘書監荀勖，又因《中經》，更著《新簿》，分為四部，總括群書。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Mo of Wei first compiled the Inner Canon; Superintendent of the Secretariat Xun Xu then built on the Inner Canon and further compiled the New Register, dividing books into four sections and gathering all texts together.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Mo of Wei first compiled the Inner Canon; Superintendent of the Secretariat Xun Xu then built on the Inner Canon and further compiled the New Register, dividing books into four sections and gathering all texts together.

sentences.zh: 一曰甲部，紀六藝及小學等書；

translations.literal: The first was Section A, recording the Six Arts and elementary learning and the like;
translations.idiomatic: The first was Section A, recording the Six Arts and elementary learning and the like;

sentences.zh: 二曰乙部，有古諸子家、近世子家、兵書、兵家、術數；

translations.literal: the second was Section B, containing ancient schools of the various masters, recent schools of the various masters, military books, military schools, and numerology;
translations.idiomatic: the second was Section B, containing ancient schools of the various masters, recent schools of the various masters, military books, military schools, and numerology;

sentences.zh: 三曰丙部，有史記、舊事、皇覽簿、雜事；

translations.literal: the third was Section C, containing historical records, old affairs, the Imperial Overview Register, and miscellaneous matters;
translations.idiomatic: the third was Section C, containing historical records, old affairs, the Imperial Overview Register, and miscellaneous matters;

sentences.zh: 四曰丁部，有詩賦、圖贊、汲塚書。

translations.literal: the fourth was Section D, containing odes and rhapsodies, illustrated encomia, and the Ji Tomb books.
translations.idiomatic: the fourth was Section D, containing odes and rhapsodies, illustrated encomia, and the Ji Tomb books.

sentences.zh: 大凡四部合二萬九千九百四十五卷。

translations.literal: In all, the four sections combined totaled twenty-nine thousand nine hundred forty-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the four sections combined totaled twenty-nine thousand nine hundred forty-five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 但錄題及言，盛以縹囊，書用緗素。

translations.literal: They only recorded titles and summaries, storing them in blue silk bags and writing on red silk.
translations.idiomatic: They only recorded titles and summaries, storing them in blue silk bags and writing on red silk.

sentences.zh: 至於作者之意，無所論辯。

translations.literal: As for the authors' intentions, there was no discussion or analysis.
translations.idiomatic: As for the authors' intentions, there was no discussion or analysis.

sentences.zh: 惠、懷之亂，京華蕩覆，渠閣文籍，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of the reigns of Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai, the capital was overturned and destroyed, and not a single text in the canal-pavilion archives survived.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of the reigns of Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai, the capital was overturned and destroyed, and not a single text in the canal-pavilion archives survived.

sentences.zh: 東晉之初，漸更鳩聚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Eastern Jin, they gradually gathered and reassembled books again.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Eastern Jin, they gradually gathered and reassembled books again.

sentences.zh: 著作郎李充以勖舊簿校之，其見存者，但有三千一十四卷。

translations.literal: Director of Composition Li Chong collated them against Xu's old register; of what survived, there were only three thousand fourteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Composition Li Chong collated them against Xu's old register; of what survived, there were only three thousand fourteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 充遂總沒眾篇之名，但以甲乙為次。

translations.literal: Chong then gathered together the names of all the texts, arranging them only by sections A and B.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then gathered together the names of all the texts, arranging them only by sections A and B.

sentences.zh: 自爾因循，無所變革。

translations.literal: From then on this practice continued without change.
translations.idiomatic: From then on this practice continued without change.

sentences.zh: 其後中朝遺書，稍流江左。

translations.literal: Afterward books from the central court gradually flowed to the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward books from the central court gradually flowed to the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉八年，秘書監謝靈運造《四部目錄》，大凡六萬四千五百八十二卷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia of the Liu Song, Superintendent of the Secretariat Xie Lingyun compiled the Four-Section Catalog; in all, sixty-four thousand five hundred eighty-two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia of the Liu Song, Superintendent of the Secretariat Xie Lingyun compiled the Four-Section Catalog; in all, sixty-four thousand five hundred eighty-two scrolls.

sentences.zh: ，秘書丞王儉又造《目錄》，大凡一萬五千七百四卷。

translations.literal: Secretariat Assistant Wang Jian also compiled a Catalog; in all, fifteen thousand seven hundred four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Assistant Wang Jian also compiled a Catalog; in all, fifteen thousand seven hundred four scrolls.

sentences.zh: 儉又別撰《七志》：一曰《經典志》，紀六藝、小學、史記、雜傳；

translations.literal: Jian also separately compiled the Seven Records: first, the Record of Classics, recording the Six Arts, elementary learning, historical records, and miscellaneous biographies;
translations.idiomatic: Jian also separately compiled the Seven Records: first, the Record of Classics, recording the Six Arts, elementary learning, historical records, and miscellaneous biographies;

sentences.zh: 二曰《諸子志》，紀今古諸子；

translations.literal: second, the Record of the Various Masters, recording ancient and modern various masters;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Record of the Various Masters, recording ancient and modern various masters;

sentences.zh: 三曰《文翰志》，紀詩賦；

translations.literal: third, the Record of Literary Writings, recording odes and rhapsodies;
translations.idiomatic: third, the Record of Literary Writings, recording odes and rhapsodies;

sentences.zh: 四曰《軍書志》，紀兵書；

translations.literal: fourth, the Record of Military Books, recording military books;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Record of Military Books, recording military books;

sentences.zh: 五曰《陰陽志》，紀陰陽圖緯；

translations.literal: fifth, the Record of Yin and Yang, recording yin-yang charts and weft texts;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the Record of Yin and Yang, recording yin-yang charts and weft texts;

sentences.zh: 六曰《術藝志》，紀方技；

translations.literal: sixth, the Record of Technical Arts, recording technical skills;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the Record of Technical Arts, recording technical skills;

sentences.zh: 七曰《圖譜志》，紀地域及圖書。

translations.literal: seventh, the Record of Charts and Registers, recording territories and books.
translations.idiomatic: seventh, the Record of Charts and Registers, recording territories and books.

sentences.zh: 其道、佛附見，合九條。

translations.literal: The Way and Buddhism were appended separately, nine sections in all.
translations.idiomatic: Daoism and Buddhism were listed in appendices, nine sections in all.

sentences.zh: 然亦不述作者之意，但於書名之下，每立一傳，而又作九篇條例，編乎首卷之中。

translations.literal: Yet he still did not set forth the authors' intentions; he only established a biography beneath each book title, and also composed nine articles of regulations, compiled in the first scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still did not explain the authors' intentions; he only added a biographical note under each title, and also wrote nine articles of regulations placed in the first scroll.

sentences.zh: 文義淺近，未為典則。

translations.literal: The literary meaning was shallow and recent, and did not serve as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: The prose was shallow and recent, and did not serve as a proper standard.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，秘書丞王亮、監謝朏，又造《四部書目》，大凡一萬八千一十卷。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era of Qi, Secretariat Assistant Wang Liang and Superintendent Xie Tiao also compiled the Four-Section Book List; in all, eighteen thousand ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era of Qi, Secretariat Assistant Wang Liang and Superintendent Xie Tiao also compiled the Four-Section Book List, totaling eighteen thousand ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 齊末兵火，延燒秘閣，經籍遺散。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi, war and fire spread to the secret pavilion, and the classics and records were lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi, war and fire spread to the secret pavilion, and the classics and records were lost and scattered.

sentences.zh: 梁初，秘書監任昉躬加部集，又於文德殿內列藏眾書，華林園中總集釋典，大凡二萬三千一百六卷，而釋氏不豫焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, Superintendent Ren Fang personally undertook the classification, and also arranged the collected books within the Hall of Cultured Virtue; in the Hua Lin Garden he gathered Buddhist scriptures together—in all, twenty-three thousand one hundred sixty scrolls, not counting Buddhist texts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Liang, Superintendent Ren Fang personally undertook the classification and arranged the collected books in the Hall of Cultured Virtue. In the Hua Lin Garden he gathered Buddhist scriptures together—twenty-three thousand one hundred sixty scrolls in all, not counting Buddhist texts.

sentences.zh: 梁有秘書監任昉、殷鈞《四部目錄》，又《文德殿目錄》。

translations.literal: Liang had the Four-Section Catalog by Superintendents Ren Fang and Yin Jun, and also the Hall of Cultured Virtue Catalog.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang dynasty produced the Four-Section Catalog by Superintendents Ren Fang and Yin Jun, and also the Hall of Cultured Virtue Catalog.

sentences.zh: 其術數之書，更為一部，使奉朝請祖暅撰其名。

translations.literal: Books on numerology were made into a separate section, with Attendant-in-Ordinary Zu Geng assigned to compile its titles.
translations.idiomatic: Books on numerology were placed in a separate section, with Attendant-in-Ordinary Zu Geng assigned to compile its titles.

sentences.zh: 故梁有《五部目錄》。

translations.literal: Thus Liang had the Five-Section Catalog.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Liang dynasty had the Five-Section Catalog.

sentences.zh: 普通中，有處士阮孝緒，沉靜寡欲，篤好墳史，博采宋、齊已來王公之家凡有書記，參校官簿，更為《七錄》：一曰《經典錄》，紀六藝；

translations.literal: In the Putong era there was the recluse Ruan Xiaoxu, quiet and free of desire, who deeply loved ancient texts and history, broadly gathered book records from the houses of kings and nobles since Song and Qi, cross-checked them against official registers, and further compiled the Seven Records: first, the Record of Classics, recording the Six Arts;
translations.idiomatic: In the Putong era there was the recluse Ruan Xiaoxu, quiet and free of desire, who deeply loved ancient texts and history. He broadly gathered book records from noble households since Song and Qi, cross-checked them against official registers, and compiled the Seven Records: first, the Record of Classics, recording the Six Arts;

sentences.zh: 二曰《記傳錄》，紀史傳；

translations.literal: second, the Record of Annals and Biographies, recording histories and biographies;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Record of Annals and Biographies, recording histories and biographies;

sentences.zh: 三曰《子兵錄》，紀子書、兵書；

translations.literal: third, the Record of Masters and Military Books, recording masters' texts and military books;
translations.idiomatic: third, the Record of Masters and Military Books, recording philosophical texts and military books;

sentences.zh: 四曰《文集錄》，紀詩賦；

translations.literal: fourth, the Record of Literary Collections, recording odes and rhapsodies;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Record of Literary Collections, recording odes and rhapsodies;

sentences.zh: 五曰《技術錄》，紀數術；

translations.literal: fifth, the Record of Technical Arts, recording numerology;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the Record of Technical Arts, recording numerology;

sentences.zh: 六曰《佛錄》；

translations.literal: sixth, the Record of Buddhism;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the Record of Buddhism;

sentences.zh: 七曰《道錄》。

translations.literal: seventh, the Record of Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: seventh, the Record of Daoism.

sentences.zh: 其分部題目，頗有次序，割析辭義，淺薄不經。

translations.literal: Its division of sections and titles had a certain order, but its analysis of meaning was shallow and unsound.
translations.idiomatic: Its division of sections and titles had a certain order, but its analysis of meaning was shallow and unsound.

sentences.zh: 梁武敦悅詩書，下化其上，四境之內，家有文史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply delighted in the Odes and Documents and transformed those below through his example above; within the four borders, every household had literary and historical books.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply delighted in the Odes and Documents and set an example from above; within the four borders, every household had literary and historical books.

sentences.zh: 元帝克平侯景，收文德之書及公私經籍，歸於江陵，大凡七萬餘卷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan defeated Hou Jing, he collected the books of the Hall of Cultured Virtue and public and private classics and records, bringing them back to Jiangling—in all, more than seventy thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan defeated Hou Jing, he collected the books of the Hall of Cultured Virtue along with public and private classics and records, bringing them back to Jiangling—more than seventy thousand scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 周師入郢，咸自焚之。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army entered Ying, they were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army entered Ying, they were all burned.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，又更鳩集，考其篇目，遺闕尚多。

translations.literal: In the Tianchen era of Chen, they again gathered and reassembled books, but examining the titles, many were still missing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianchen era of Chen, they again gathered and reassembled books, but examining the titles, many were still missing.

sentences.zh: 其中原則戰爭相尋，干戈是務，文教之盛，苻、姚而已。

translations.literal: Among them, in the Central Plains war followed war and arms were the chief concern; only under Former Qin and Later Qin did literary culture flourish.
translations.idiomatic: In the Central Plains, war followed war and arms were the chief concern; only under Former Qin and Later Qin did literary culture flourish.

sentences.zh: 宋武入關，收其圖籍，府藏所有，才四千卷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song entered the passes, he collected their charts and records; what the treasury held amounted to only four thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song entered the passes, he collected their charts and records; the treasury held only four thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 赤軸青紙，文字古拙。

translations.literal: Red axles and blue paper; the writing was ancient and crude.
translations.idiomatic: They had red axles and blue paper, and the writing was ancient and crude.

sentences.zh: 後魏始都燕代，南略中原，粗收經史，未能全具。

translations.literal: Later Wei first established its capital at Yan and Dai, pushed south into the Central Plains, and roughly collected classics and histories, but could not fully assemble them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei first established its capital at Yan and Dai, pushed south into the Central Plains, and roughly collected classics and histories, but could not fully assemble them.

sentences.zh: 孝文徙都洛邑，借書于齊，秘府之中，稍以充實。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, he borrowed books from Qi, and the secret repository gradually became fuller.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, he borrowed books from Qi, and the secret repository gradually became fuller.

sentences.zh: 暨於爾硃之亂，散落人間。

translations.literal: By the time of the Erzhu turmoil, they were scattered among the people.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Erzhu turmoil, they were scattered among the people.

sentences.zh: 後齊遷鄴，頗更搜聚，迄於天統、武平，校寫不輟。

translations.literal: Later, when Northern Qi moved to Ye, they searched and gathered further; down to the Tiantong and Wuping eras, collation and copying never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Northern Qi moved to Ye, they searched and gathered further; down to the Tiantong and Wuping eras, collation and copying never ceased.

sentences.zh: 後周始基關右，外逼強鄰，戎馬生郊，日不暇給。

translations.literal: Later Zhou first established its base in the Guanzhong region, pressed from without by powerful neighbors, with war-horses in the suburbs and no leisure even for a day's work.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou first established its base in the Guanzhong region, pressed from without by powerful neighbors, with war-horses in the suburbs and no leisure even for a day's work.

sentences.zh: 保定之始，書止八千，後稍加增，方盈萬卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoding era, books numbered only eight thousand; afterward they were gradually increased until they barely reached ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoding era, books numbered only eight thousand; afterward they were gradually increased until they barely reached ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，先封書府，所加舊本，才至五千。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Northern Qi, he first sealed the book repository; the old texts added amounted to only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Northern Qi, he first sealed the book repository; the old texts added amounted to only five thousand.

sentences.zh: 隋，秘書監牛弘表請分遣使人，搜訪異本。

translations.literal: In Sui, Superintendent of the Secretariat Niu Hong submitted a memorial requesting that emissaries be dispatched separately to search for variant copies.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui, Superintendent of the Secretariat Niu Hong submitted a memorial requesting that emissaries be dispatched separately to search for variant copies.

sentences.zh: 每書一卷，賞絹一匹，校寫既定，本即歸主。

translations.literal: For each scroll of a book, one bolt of silk was given as reward; once collation and copying were finished, the original was returned to its owner.
translations.idiomatic: For each scroll of a book, one bolt of silk was given as reward; once collation and copying were finished, the original was returned to its owner.

sentences.zh: 於是民間異書，往往間出。

translations.literal: Thereupon variant books among the people often appeared from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon variant books among the people often appeared from time to time.

sentences.zh: 及平陳已後，經籍漸備。

translations.literal: After Chen was pacified, the classics and records gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, the classics and records gradually became complete.

sentences.zh: 檢其所得，多太建時書，紙墨不精，書亦拙惡。

translations.literal: Examining what was obtained, most were books from the Taijian era; the paper and ink were poor, and the writing was also crude and bad.
translations.idiomatic: Examining what was obtained, most were books from the Taijian era; the paper and ink were poor, and the writing was also crude and bad.

sentences.zh: 於是總集編次，存為古本。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were gathered together, arranged in order, and preserved as old texts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they were gathered together, arranged in order, and preserved as old texts.

sentences.zh: 召天下工書之士，京兆韋霈、南陽杜頵等，于秘書內補續殘缺，為正副二本，藏于宮中，其餘以實秘書內、外之閣，凡三萬餘卷。

translations.literal: They summoned masters of calligraphy from throughout the realm—Wei Pei of Jingzhao, Du Yun of Nanyang, and others—and within the Secretariat supplemented and restored what was missing, making principal and duplicate copies stored in the palace; the rest filled the inner and outer pavilions of the Secretariat—in all, more than thirty thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned masters of calligraphy from throughout the realm—Wei Pei of Jingzhao, Du Yun of Nanyang, and others—and within the Secretariat supplemented and restored what was missing, making principal and duplicate copies stored in the palace. The rest filled the inner and outer pavilions of the Secretariat—more than thirty thousand scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，秘閣之書，限寫五十副本，分為三品：上品紅琉璃軸，中品紺琉璃軸，下品漆軸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, books in the secret pavilion were limited to fifty copied sets, divided into three grades: top grade with red glass axles, middle grade with dark blue glass axles, and lower grade with lacquer axles.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, books in the secret pavilion were limited to fifty copied sets, divided into three grades: top grade with red glass axles, middle grade with dark blue glass axles, and lower grade with lacquer axles.

sentences.zh: 于東都觀文殿東西廂構屋以貯之，東屋藏甲乙，西屋藏丙丁。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital's Hall for Viewing Literature, buildings were constructed in the east and west wings to store them: the east wing stored sections A and B, the west wing stored sections C and D.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital's Hall for Viewing Literature, buildings were constructed in the east and west wings to store them: the east wing stored sections A and B, the west wing stored sections C and D.

sentences.zh: 又聚魏已來古跡名畫，於殿後起二台，東曰妙楷台，藏古跡；

translations.literal: They also gathered ancient traces and famous paintings since Wei, and behind the hall erected two platforms: the east was called the Platform of Exquisite Models, storing ancient traces;
translations.idiomatic: They also gathered ancient traces and famous paintings since Wei, and behind the hall erected two platforms: the east was called the Platform of Exquisite Models, storing ancient traces;

sentences.zh: 西曰寶跡台，藏古畫。

translations.literal: the west was called the Platform of Precious Traces, storing ancient paintings.
translations.idiomatic: the west was called the Platform of Precious Traces, storing ancient paintings.

sentences.zh: 又於內道場集道、佛經，別撰目錄。

translations.literal: They also gathered Daoist and Buddhist scriptures at the Inner Way Place and separately compiled a catalog.
translations.idiomatic: They also gathered Daoist and Buddhist scriptures at the Inner Way Place and separately compiled a catalog.

sentences.zh: 大唐，克平偽鄭，盡收其圖書及古跡焉。

translations.literal: When the Great Tang conquered the false Zheng regime, it fully collected their charts, books, and ancient traces.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Tang conquered the false Zheng regime, it fully collected their charts, books, and ancient traces.

sentences.zh: 命司農少卿宋遵貴載之以船，溯河西上，將致京師。

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Song Zungui to load them onto boats and send them up the Yellow River westward, intending to bring them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Song Zungui to load them onto boats and send them up the Yellow River westward, intending to bring them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 行經底柱，多被漂沒，其所存者，十不一二。

translations.literal: Passing Di Gorge, many were washed away and sunk; of what survived, not one in ten remained.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Di Gorge, many were washed away and sunk; of what survived, not one in ten remained.

sentences.zh: 其《目錄》亦為所漸濡，時有殘缺。

translations.literal: The Catalog was also gradually soaked by the water, and at times had gaps and omissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Catalog was also gradually soaked by the water, and at times had gaps and omissions.

sentences.zh: 今考見存，分為四部，合條為一萬四千四百六十六部，有八萬九千六百六十六卷。

translations.literal: Now examining what survives, they are divided into four sections, combined into fourteen thousand four hundred sixty-six titles, with eighty-nine thousand six hundred sixty-six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Now examining what survives, they are divided into four sections, combined into fourteen thousand four hundred sixty-six titles, with eighty-nine thousand six hundred sixty-six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其舊錄所取，文義淺俗、無益教理者，並刪去之。

translations.literal: What the old register took in but whose meaning was shallow and vulgar and of no benefit to teaching and principle—all were deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Entries from the old register whose meaning was shallow and vulgar and of no benefit to teaching and principle were all deleted.

sentences.zh: 其舊錄所遺，辭義可采，有所弘益者，咸附入之。

translations.literal: What the old register omitted but whose meaning was worth adopting and could broaden and benefit—all were appended.
translations.idiomatic: Entries the old register omitted but whose meaning was worth adopting and could broaden and benefit were all appended.

sentences.zh: 遠覽馬史、班書，近觀王、阮志、錄，挹其風流體制，削其浮雜鄙俚，離其疏遠，合其近密，約文緒義，凡五十五篇，各列本條之下，以備《經籍志》。

translations.literal: Looking far at the histories of Sima and Ban, and near at the records and catalogs of Wang and Ruan, drawing on their style and structure, cutting away the frivolous, vulgar, and coarse, separating what was remote, joining what was close and dense, condensing the text and clarifying the meaning—in all fifty-five sections, each listed under its own entry, to complete the Bibliographic Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Looking far at the histories of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, and near at the records and catalogs of Wang and Ruan, I drew on their style and structure, cut away the frivolous, vulgar, and coarse, separated what was remote, joined what was close and dense, and condensed the text and clarified the meaning—in all fifty-five sections, each listed under its own entry, to complete the Bibliographic Treatise.

sentences.zh: 雖未能研幾探賾，窮極幽隱，庶乎弘道設教，可以無遺闕焉。

translations.literal: Although I have not been able to probe the subtle and explore the hidden, reaching the utmost depths, I hope that in spreading the Way and establishing teaching nothing may be left out.
translations.idiomatic: Although I have not been able to probe the subtle and explore the hidden, reaching the utmost depths, I hope that in spreading the Way and establishing teaching nothing may be left out.

sentences.zh: 夫仁義禮智，所以治國也，方技數術，所以治身也；

translations.literal: Benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom are what govern the state; technical arts and numerology are what govern the body;
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom are what govern the state; technical arts and numerology are what govern the body;

sentences.zh: 諸子為經籍之鼓吹，文章乃政化之黼黻，皆為治之具也。

translations.literal: The various masters are the heralds of the classics and records, and literary writings are the adornments of government and transformation—all are instruments of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The various masters are the heralds of the classics and records, and literary writings are the adornments of government and transformation—all are instruments of governance.

sentences.zh: 故列之於此志云。

translations.literal: Therefore they are listed in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they are listed in this treatise.

translations.idiomatic: Genealogy of the Book of Changes, one scroll.

translations.literal: Above: sixty-nine titles, five hundred fifty-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Above: sixty-nine titles, five hundred fifty-one scrolls.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合九十四部，八百二十九卷。

translations.literal: Counting lost books together, ninety-four titles, eight hundred twenty-nine scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Counting lost books together, ninety-four titles, eight hundred twenty-nine scrolls.

sentences.zh: :昔宓羲氏始畫八卦，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情，蓋因而重之，為六十四卦。

translations.literal: In antiquity Fu Xi first drew the eight trigrams to communicate the virtue of the spirits and to classify the feelings of the myriad things; he then doubled them to make sixty-four hexagrams.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Fu Xi first drew the eight trigrams to communicate the virtue of the spirits and to classify the feelings of the myriad things, then doubled them to make sixty-four hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 及乎三代，實為三《易》，夏曰《連山》；

translations.literal: Down to the Three Dynasties, there were in fact three Changes: Xia had the Linked Mountains;
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Three Dynasties, there were in fact three Changes: Xia had the Linked Mountains;

sentences.zh: 殷曰《歸藏》；

translations.literal: Yin had the Hidden Storehouse;
translations.idiomatic: Yin had the Hidden Storehouse;

sentences.zh: 周文王作卦辭，謂之《周易》。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou composed the hexagram statements, calling it the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou composed the hexagram statements, calling it the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 周公又作《爻辭》，孔子為《彖》、《象》、《繫辭》、《文言》、《序卦》、《說卦》、《雜卦》，而子夏為之傳。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou also composed the line statements; Confucius wrote the Judgments, Images, Appended Statements, Wenyan, Sequence of Hexagrams, Explanation of the Trigrams, and Miscellaneous Hexagrams, and Zixia transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou also composed the line statements; Confucius wrote the Judgments, Images, Appended Statements, Wenyan, Sequence of Hexagrams, Explanation of the Trigrams, and Miscellaneous Hexagrams, and Zixia transmitted it.

sentences.zh: 及秦焚書，《周易》獨以卜筮得存，唯失《說卦》三篇。

translations.literal: When Qin burned the books, the Book of Changes alone survived because of divination, but the three sections of the Explanation of the Trigrams were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin burned the books, the Book of Changes alone survived because of divination, but the three sections of the Explanation of the Trigrams were lost.

sentences.zh: 後河內女子得之。

translations.literal: Later a woman of Henei recovered them.
translations.idiomatic: Later a woman of Henei recovered them.

sentences.zh: 漢初，傳《易》者有田何，何授丁寬，寬授田王孫，王孫授沛人施仇、東海孟喜、琅邪梁丘賀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, those who transmitted the Changes included Tian He; He taught Ding Kuan; Kuan taught Tian Wangsun; Wangsun taught Shi Chou of Pei, Meng Xi of Donghai, and Liangqiu He of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, those who transmitted the Changes included Tian He; He taught Ding Kuan; Kuan taught Tian Wangsun; Wangsun taught Shi Chou of Pei, Meng Xi of Donghai, and Liangqiu He of Langye.

sentences.zh: 由是有施、孟、梁丘之學。

translations.literal: Hence there were the schools of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there were the schools of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu.

sentences.zh: 又有東郡京房，自雲受《易》于梁國焦延壽，別為京氏學。

translations.literal: There was also Jing Fang of Dongjun, who claimed to have received the Changes from Jiao Yanshou of Liang, forming a separate Jing school.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Jing Fang of Dongjun, who claimed to have received the Changes from Jiao Yanshou of Liang, forming a separate Jing school.

sentences.zh: 嘗立，後罷。

translations.literal: It was once established, then later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was once established, then later abolished.

sentences.zh: 後漢施、孟、梁丘、京氏，凡四家並立，而傳者甚眾。

translations.literal: In Later Han the Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing schools—four in all—were simultaneously established, and those who transmitted them were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han the Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing schools—four in all—were simultaneously established, and those who transmitted them were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 漢初又有東萊費直傳《易》，其本皆古字，號曰《古文易》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han there was also Fei Zhi of Donglai, who transmitted the Changes; his text was entirely in ancient characters, called the Old Text Changes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han there was also Fei Zhi of Donglai, who transmitted the Changes; his text was entirely in ancient characters, called the Old Text Changes.

sentences.zh: 以授琅邪王璜，璜授沛人高相，相以授子康及蘭陵母將永。

translations.literal: He taught Wang Huang of Langye; Huang taught Gao Xiang of Pei; Xiang taught his son Kang and Jiang Yong of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He taught Wang Huang of Langye; Huang taught Gao Xiang of Pei; Xiang taught his son Kang and Jiang Yong of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 故有費氏之學，行於人間，而未得立。

translations.literal: Hence there was the Fei school, circulating among the people but not established at court.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there was the Fei school, circulating among the people but not established at court.

sentences.zh: 後漢陳元、鄭眾，皆傳費氏之學。

translations.literal: In Later Han Chen Yuan and Zheng Zhong both transmitted the Fei school.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han Chen Yuan and Zheng Zhong both transmitted the Fei school.

sentences.zh: 馬融又為其傳，以授鄭玄。

translations.literal: Ma Rong also transmitted it and taught Zheng Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong also transmitted it and taught Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄作《易注》，荀爽又作《易傳》。

translations.literal: Xuan composed a Commentary on the Changes, and Xun Shuang also composed a Commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan composed a Commentary on the Changes, and Xun Shuang also composed a Commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 魏代王肅、王弼，並為之注。

translations.literal: In Wei, Wang Su and Wang Bi both annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Wang Su and Wang Bi both annotated it.

sentences.zh: 自是費氏大興，高氏遂衰。

translations.literal: From this time the Fei school flourished greatly and the Gao school declined.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the Fei school flourished greatly and the Gao school declined.

sentences.zh: 梁丘、施氏、高氏，亡於西晉。

translations.literal: The Liangqiu, Shi, and Gao schools perished in Western Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangqiu, Shi, and Gao schools perished in Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 孟氏、京氏，有書無師。

translations.literal: The Meng and Jing schools had books but no teachers.
translations.idiomatic: The Meng and Jing schools had books but no teachers.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳鄭玄、王弼二注，列于國學。

translations.literal: In Liang and Chen the two commentaries of Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi were listed in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang and Chen the two commentaries of Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi were listed in the National University.

sentences.zh: 齊代唯傳鄭義。

translations.literal: In Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.

sentences.zh: 至隋，王注盛行，鄭學浸微，今殆絕矣。

translations.literal: By Sui, Wang's commentary prevailed and Zheng's learning gradually faded; today it is nearly extinct.
translations.idiomatic: By Sui, Wang's commentary prevailed and Zheng's learning gradually faded; today it is nearly extinct.

sentences.zh: 《歸藏》，漢初已亡，案晉《中經》有之，唯載卜筮，不似聖人之旨。

translations.literal: The Hidden Storehouse was already lost at the beginning of Han; examining Jin's Inner Canon, it was present, but it recorded only divination and did not resemble the purport of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Storehouse was already lost at the beginning of Han; examining Jin's Inner Canon, it was present, but it recorded only divination and did not resemble the purport of the sages.

sentences.zh: 以本卦尚存，故取貫于《周易》之首，以備《殷易》之缺。

translations.literal: Because the original hexagrams still survive, it is placed at the head of the Book of Changes to supply what is missing from the Yin Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Because the original hexagrams still survive, it is placed at the head of the Book of Changes to supply what is missing from the Yin Changes.

sentences.zh: 書《古文尚書》十三卷漢臨淮太守孔安國傳。

translations.literal: Classic: Documents—The Old Text Documents in thirteen scrolls, transmitted by Kong Anguo, Administrator of Huaihai in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Classic: Documents—The Old Text Documents in thirteen scrolls, transmitted by Kong Anguo, Administrator of Huaihai in Han.

sentences.zh: 《今字尚書》十四卷孔安國傳。

translations.literal: The Documents in Modern Characters in fourteen scrolls, transmitted by Kong Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents in Modern Characters in fourteen scrolls, transmitted by Kong Anguo.

sentences.zh: 《尚書》十一卷馬融注。

translations.idiomatic: Above: 三十二部，二百四十七卷.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合四十一部，共二百九十六卷。

translations.idiomatic: Including lost books, totaling 四十一部 titles and 共二百九十六卷 scrolls.

sentences.zh: :《書》之所興，蓋與文字俱起。

translations.literal: The rise of the Documents is said to have begun together with writing.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of the Documents is said to have begun together with writing.

sentences.zh: 孔子觀《書》周室，得虞、夏、商、週四代之典，刪其善者，上自虞，下至周，為百篇，編而序之。

translations.literal: Confucius, examining the Documents of the Zhou royal house, obtained the canonical records of the four dynasties Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou; he edited what was good, from Yu above down to Zhou below, making one hundred chapters, which he arranged and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, examining the Documents of the Zhou royal house, obtained the canonical records of the four dynasties Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou. He edited what was good, from Yu above down to Zhou below, making one hundred chapters, which he arranged and ordered.

sentences.zh: 遭秦滅學，至漢，唯濟南伏生口傳二十八篇。

translations.literal: When Qin extinguished learning, down to Han only Fu Sheng of Jinan orally transmitted twenty-eight chapters.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin extinguished learning, by Han times only Fu Sheng of Jinan orally transmitted twenty-eight chapters.

sentences.zh: 又河內女子得《泰誓》一篇，獻之。

translations.literal: Also a woman of Henei obtained the Tai Declaration in one chapter and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Also a woman of Henei obtained the Tai Declaration in one chapter and presented it.

sentences.zh: 伏生作《尚書傳》四十一篇，以授同郡張生，張生授千乘歐陽生，歐陽生授同郡倪寬，寬授歐陽生之子，世世傳之，至曾孫歐陽高，謂之《尚書》歐陽之學。

translations.literal: Fu Sheng composed a Tradition of the Documents in forty-one chapters and taught Zhang Sheng of the same commandery; Zhang Sheng taught Ouyang Sheng of Qiancheng; Ouyang Sheng taught Ni Kuan of the same commandery; Kuan taught Ouyang Sheng's son, and it was transmitted for generations down to great-grandson Ouyang Gao—this was called the Ouyang school of the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng composed a Tradition of the Documents in forty-one chapters and taught Zhang Sheng of the same commandery; Zhang Sheng taught Ouyang Sheng of Qiancheng; Ouyang Sheng taught Ni Kuan of the same commandery; Kuan taught Ouyang Sheng's son, and it was transmitted for generations down to great-grandson Ouyang Gao—this was called the Ouyang school of the Documents.

sentences.zh: 又有夏侯都尉，受業于張生，以授族子始昌，始昌傳族子勝，為大夏侯之學。

translations.literal: There was also Commandant of the Guard Xiahou, who received instruction from Zhang Sheng and taught his clansman Shichang; Shichang taught his clansman Sheng, forming the Great Xiahou school.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Commandant of the Guard Xiahou, who received instruction from Zhang Sheng and taught his clansman Shichang; Shichang taught his clansman Sheng, forming the Great Xiahou school.

sentences.zh: 勝傳從子建，別為小夏侯之學。

translations.literal: Sheng taught his nephew Jian, who separately formed the Lesser Xiahou school.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng taught his nephew Jian, who separately formed the Lesser Xiahou school.

sentences.zh: 故有歐陽，大、小夏侯，三家並立。

translations.literal: Hence the Ouyang, Great Xiahou, and Lesser Xiahou schools were all established.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Ouyang, Great Xiahou, and Lesser Xiahou schools were all established.

sentences.zh: 訖漢東京，相傳不絕，而歐陽最盛。

translations.literal: Down to Eastern Han at Luoyang, transmission never ceased, and Ouyang was most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Eastern Han at Luoyang, transmission never ceased, and the Ouyang school was most flourishing.

sentences.zh: 初漢武帝時，魯恭王壞孔子舊宅，得其末孫惠所藏之書，字皆古文。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, King Gong of Lu destroyed Confucius's old residence and obtained books stored by his last descendant Hui; the characters were all ancient script.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, King Gong of Lu destroyed Confucius's old residence and obtained books stored by his last descendant Hui; the characters were all in ancient script.

sentences.zh: 孔安國以今文校之，得二十五篇。

translations.literal: Kong Anguo collated them against the modern script and obtained twenty-five chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo collated them against the modern script and obtained twenty-five chapters.

sentences.zh: 其《泰誓》與河內女子所獻不同。

translations.literal: Its Tai Declaration differed from what the woman of Henei presented.
translations.idiomatic: Its Tai Declaration differed from what the woman of Henei presented.

sentences.zh: 又濟南伏生所誦，有五篇相合。

translations.literal: Of what Fu Sheng of Jinan recited, five chapters matched.
translations.idiomatic: Of what Fu Sheng of Jinan recited, five chapters matched.

sentences.zh: 安國並依古文，開其篇第，以隸古字寫之，合成五十八篇。

translations.literal: Anguo followed the ancient script throughout, opened their chapter sequence, wrote them in clerical ancient characters, and combined them into fifty-eight chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo followed the ancient script throughout, opened their chapter sequence, wrote them in clerical ancient characters, and combined them into fifty-eight chapters.

sentences.zh: 其餘篇簡錯亂，不可複讀，並送之官府。

translations.literal: The remaining bamboo slips were confused and could not be read again; all were sent to the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bamboo slips were confused and could not be read again; all were sent to the government offices.

sentences.zh: 安國又為五十八篇作傳，會巫蠱事起，不得奏上，私傳其業于都尉朝，朝授膠東庸生，謂之《尚書古文》之學，而未得立。

translations.literal: Anguo also composed a commentary for fifty-eight chapters, but when the witchcraft affair arose, he could not submit it to the throne; he privately transmitted his craft to Commandant Chao; Chao taught Yong Sheng of Jiaodong—this was called the Old Text Documents school, but it was not established at court.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo also composed a commentary for fifty-eight chapters, but when the witchcraft affair arose, he could not submit it to the throne. He privately transmitted his craft to Commandant Chao; Chao taught Yong Sheng of Jiaodong. This was called the Old Text Documents school, but it was not established at court.

sentences.zh: 後漢扶風杜林，傳《古文尚書》，同郡賈逵為之作訓，馬融作傳，鄭玄亦為之注。

translations.literal: In Later Han, Du Lin of Fufeng transmitted the Old Text Documents; Jia Kui of the same commandery composed exegesis for it; Ma Rong composed a tradition; Zheng Xuan also annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Du Lin of Fufeng transmitted the Old Text Documents; Jia Kui of the same commandery composed exegesis for it; Ma Rong composed a tradition; Zheng Xuan also annotated it.

sentences.zh: 然其所傳，唯二十九篇，又雜以今文，非孔舊本。

translations.literal: Yet what was transmitted had only twenty-nine chapters, mixed with modern script, and was not Confucius's old text.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what was transmitted had only twenty-nine chapters, mixed with modern script, and was not Confucius's old text.

sentences.zh: 自余絕無師說。

translations.literal: Beyond this there was absolutely no teacher's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this there was absolutely no teacher's explanation.

sentences.zh: :晉世秘府所存，有《古文尚書》經文，今無有傳者。

translations.literal: In the Jin era what the secret repository preserved was the text of the Old Text Documents; today there is no one who transmits it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin era what the secret repository preserved was the text of the Old Text Documents; today there is no one who transmits it.

sentences.zh: 及永嘉之亂，歐陽，大、小夏侯《尚書》並亡。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Yongjia, the Ouyang and Great and Lesser Xiahou versions of the Documents all perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Yongjia, the Ouyang and Great and Lesser Xiahou versions of the Documents all perished.

sentences.zh: 濟南伏生之傳，唯劉向父子所著《五行傳》是其本法，而又多乖戾。

translations.literal: Of Fu Sheng of Jinan's transmission, only the Treatise on the Five Processes composed by Liu Xiang and his son is the correct method, yet it too contains many contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: Of Fu Sheng of Jinan's transmission, only the Treatise on the Five Processes composed by Liu Xiang and his son is the correct method, yet it too contains many contradictions.

sentences.zh: 至東晉，豫章內史梅賾，始得安國之傳，奏之，時又闕《舜典》一篇。

translations.literal: By Eastern Jin, Mei Ze, Administrator of Yuzhang, first obtained Anguo's transmission and submitted it; at the time the Canon of Shun in one chapter was still missing.
translations.idiomatic: By Eastern Jin, Mei Ze, Administrator of Yuzhang, first obtained Anguo's transmission and submitted it; at the time the Canon of Shun in one chapter was still missing.

sentences.zh: 齊建武中，吳姚方興於大桁市得其書，奏上，比馬、鄭所注多二十八字，於是始列國學。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi, Yao Fangxing of Wu obtained the book in the market at Daxing and submitted it; compared with the annotations of Ma and Zheng it had twenty-eight more characters, and thus it was first listed in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era of Qi, Yao Fangxing of Wu obtained the book in the market at Daxing and submitted it; compared with the annotations of Ma and Zheng it had twenty-eight more characters, and thus it was first listed in the National University.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳所講，有孔、鄭二家，齊代唯傳鄭義。

translations.literal: What was lectured on in Liang and Chen included the Kong and Zheng schools; in Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: What was lectured on in Liang and Chen included the Kong and Zheng schools; in Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.

sentences.zh: 至隋，孔、鄭並行，而鄭氏甚微。

translations.literal: By Sui, Kong and Zheng were both current, but the Zheng school was very weak.
translations.idiomatic: By Sui, Kong and Zheng were both current, but the Zheng school was very weak.

sentences.zh: 自餘所存，無複師說。

translations.literal: Of what else survives, there is no longer any teacher's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Of what else survives, there is no longer any teacher's explanation.

sentences.zh: 又有《尚書逸篇》，出於齊、梁之間，考其篇目，似孔壁中書之殘缺者，故附《尚書》之末。

translations.literal: There was also lost Chapters of the Documents, 出於齊、梁之間，考其篇目，似孔壁中書之殘缺者，故附《尚書》之末, incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: There was also lost Chapters of the Documents, 出於齊、梁之間，考其篇目，似孔壁中書之殘缺者，故附《尚書》之末, incomplete.

translations.idiomatic: Classic: Odes—韓Classic: Odes, 22 scrolls, Han commentarial glosses by 常山太傅韓嬰，薛氏.
