sentences.zh: :《詩》者，所以導達心靈，歌詠情志者也。

translations.literal: The Odes are what guide and express the mind and spirit, singing and chanting feelings and intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes are what guide and express the mind and spirit, singing and chanting feelings and intent.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「在心為志，發言為詩。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "What is in the heart is intent; what is spoken forth is an ode."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: "What is in the heart is intent; what is spoken forth is an ode."

sentences.zh: 」上古人淳俗朴，情志未惑。

translations.literal: The ancients were pure and customs simple; feelings and intent were not yet confused.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients were pure and customs simple; feelings and intent were not yet confused.

sentences.zh: 其後君尊於上，臣卑於下，面稱為諂，目諫為謗，故誦美譏惡，以諷刺之。

translations.literal: Afterward the ruler was honored above and ministers were humble below; face-to-face praise was flattery and eye-to-eye remonstrance was slander, so chanting beauty and ridiculing evil served as satire.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the ruler was honored above and ministers were humble below; face-to-face praise was flattery and eye-to-eye remonstrance was slander, so chanting beauty and ridiculing evil served as satire.

sentences.zh: 初但歌詠而已，後之君子，因被管弦，以存勸戒。

translations.literal: At first they only sang and chanted; later gentlemen set them to strings and pipes to preserve admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At first they only sang and chanted; later gentlemen set them to strings and pipes to preserve admonition.

sentences.zh: 夏、殷已上，詩多不存。

translations.literal: Before Xia and Yin, most odes do not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xia and Yin, most odes do not survive.

sentences.zh: 周氏始自後稷，而公劉克篤前烈，太王肇基王跡，文王光昭前緒，武王克平殷亂，成王、周公化至太平，誦美盛德，踵武相繼。

translations.literal: The Zhou house began with Hou Ji; Duke Liu solidified earlier achievements; Grand King laid the foundation of royal traces; King Wen glorified earlier accomplishments; King Wu conquered and pacified Yin's disorder; King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou transformed until Great Peace—they chanted beautiful virtue, following in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou house began with Hou Ji; Duke Liu solidified earlier achievements; Grand King laid the foundation of royal traces; King Wen glorified earlier accomplishments; King Wu conquered and pacified Yin's disorder; King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou transformed until Great Peace—they chanted beautiful virtue, following in succession.

sentences.zh: 幽、厲板蕩，怨刺並興。

translations.literal: Under You and Li there was turmoil and collapse; resentment and satire arose together.
translations.idiomatic: Under You and Li there was turmoil and collapse; resentment and satire arose together.

sentences.zh: 其後王澤竭而詩亡，魯太師摯次而錄之。

translations.literal: Afterward the king's beneficence was exhausted and the odes perished; Grand Master Zhi of Lu arranged and recorded them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the king's beneficence was exhausted and the odes perished; Grand Master Zhi of Lu arranged and recorded them.

sentences.zh: 孔子刪詩，上采商，下取魯，凡三百篇。

translations.literal: Confucius edited the odes, taking from above the Shang and from below Lu—in all three hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius edited the odes, taking from above the Shang and from below Lu—in all three hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 至秦，獨以為諷誦，不滅。

translations.literal: Down to Qin, they alone survived as material for recitation and were not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Qin, they alone survived as material for recitation and were not destroyed.

sentences.zh: 漢初，有魯人申公，受《詩》于浮丘伯，作詁訓，是為《魯詩》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo and composed glosses—this was the Lu Odes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo and composed glosses—this was the Lu Odes.

sentences.zh: 齊人轅固生亦傳《詩》，是為《齊詩》。

translations.literal: Yuan Gusheng of Qi also transmitted the Odes—this was the Qi Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gusheng of Qi also transmitted the Odes—this was the Qi Odes.

sentences.zh: 燕人韓嬰亦傳《詩》，是為《韓詩》。

translations.literal: Han Ying of Yan also transmitted the Odes—this was the Han Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ying of Yan also transmitted the Odes—this was the Han Odes.

sentences.zh: 終於後漢，三家並立。

translations.literal: Down to Later Han, three schools were all established.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Later Han, three schools were all established.

sentences.zh: 漢初，又有趙人毛萇善《詩》，自雲子夏所傳，作《詁訓傳》，是為《毛詩》古學，而未得立。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, there was also Mao Chang of Zhao, skilled in the Odes, who claimed transmission from Zixia and composed a Gloss and Tradition—this was the old learning of the Mao Odes, but it was not established at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, there was also Mao Chang of Zhao, skilled in the Odes, who claimed transmission from Zixia and composed a Gloss and Tradition—this was the old learning of the Mao Odes, but it was not established at court.

sentences.zh: 後漢有九江謝曼卿，善《毛詩》，又為之訓。

translations.literal: In Later Han there was Xie Manqing of Jiujiang, skilled in the Mao Odes, who also composed exegesis for it.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han there was Xie Manqing of Jiujiang, skilled in the Mao Odes, who also composed exegesis for it.

sentences.zh: 東海衛敬仲，受學於曼卿。

translations.literal: Wei Jingzhong of Donghai received instruction from Manqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingzhong of Donghai received instruction from Manqing.

sentences.zh: 先儒相承，謂之《毛詩》。

translations.literal: Earlier Confucians transmitted by succession called it the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Confucians transmitted by succession called it the Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 序，子夏所創，毛公及敬仲又加潤益。

translations.literal: The Preface was created by Zixia; Lord Mao and Jingzhong further refined and enriched it.
translations.idiomatic: The Preface was created by Zixia; Lord Mao and Jingzhong further refined and enriched it.

sentences.zh: 鄭眾、賈逵、馬融，並作《毛詩傳》，鄭玄作《毛詩箋》。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui, and Ma Rong all composed traditions of the Mao Odes; Zheng Xuan composed the Mao Odes Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui, and Ma Rong all composed traditions of the Mao Odes; Zheng Xuan composed the Mao Odes Commentary.

sentences.zh: 《齊詩》，魏代已亡；

translations.literal: The Qi Odes were already lost in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi Odes were already lost in Wei.

sentences.zh: 《魯詩》亡於西晉；

translations.literal: The Lu Odes perished in Western Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu Odes perished in Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 《韓詩》雖存，無傳之者。

translations.literal: Though the Han Odes survived, there was no one to transmit them.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Han Odes survived, there was no one to transmit them.

sentences.zh: 唯《毛詩鄭箋》，至今獨立。

translations.literal: Only the Zheng Commentary on the Mao Odes stands alone to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Zheng Commentary on the Mao Odes stands alone to the present.

sentences.zh: 又有《業詩》，奉朝請業遵所注，立義多異，世所不行。

sentences.zh: :自大道既隱，天下為家，先王制其夫婦、父子、君臣、上下、親疏之節。

translations.literal: When the Great Way was already hidden, All-under-Heaven became a family; the earlier kings established norms for husband and wife, father and son, ruler and minister, superior and inferior, close and distant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Way was already hidden, All-under-Heaven became a family; the earlier kings established norms for husband and wife, father and son, ruler and minister, superior and inferior, close and distant.

sentences.zh: 至於三代，損益不同。

translations.literal: Down to the Three Dynasties, additions and subtractions differed.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Three Dynasties, additions and subtractions differed.

sentences.zh: 周衰，諸侯僭忒，惡其害己，多被焚削。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, feudal lords overstepped and transgressed; hating that rites harmed themselves, many were burned and cut away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, feudal lords overstepped and transgressed; hating that rites harmed themselves, many were burned and cut away.

sentences.zh: 自孔子時，已不能具，至秦而頓滅。

translations.literal: Already in Confucius's time they could not be complete; by Qin they suddenly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Already in Confucius's time they could not be complete; by Qin they suddenly perished.

sentences.zh: 漢初，有高堂生傳十七篇，又有古經，出於淹中，而河間獻王好古愛學，收集餘燼，得而獻之，合五十六篇，並威儀之事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Gao Tang transmitted seventeen chapters; there was also an old classic from Yanzhong; King Xian of Hejian loved antiquity and learning, gathered what remained from the ashes, obtained and presented them—fifty-six chapters in all, including matters of ritual decorum.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Gao Tang transmitted seventeen chapters; there was also an old classic from Yanzhong; King Xian of Hejian loved antiquity and learning, gathered what remained from the ashes, obtained and presented them—fifty-six chapters in all, including matters of ritual decorum.

sentences.zh: 而又得《司馬穰苴兵法》一百五十五篇，及《明堂陰陽》之記，並無敢傳之者。

translations.literal: 而又得司馬穰苴兵法一百五十五篇，及明堂陰陽之記，並無敢傳之者。.
translations.idiomatic: 而又得司馬穰苴兵法一百五十五篇，及明堂陰陽之記，並無敢傳之者。.

sentences.zh: 唯古經十七篇與高堂生所傳不殊，而字多異。

translations.literal: Only the seventeen chapters of the old classic did not differ from what Gao Tang transmitted, though the characters differed in many places.
translations.idiomatic: Only the seventeen chapters of the old classic did not differ from what Gao Tang transmitted, though the characters differed in many places.

sentences.zh: 自高堂生至宣帝時後蒼，最明其業，乃為《曲台記》。

translations.literal: 自高堂生至宣帝時後蒼，最明其業，乃為曲台記。.
translations.idiomatic: 自高堂生至宣帝時後蒼，最明其業，乃為曲台記。.

sentences.zh: 蒼授梁人戴德，及德從兄子聖、沛人慶普，於是有大戴、小戴、慶氏，三家並立。

translations.literal: Cang taught Dai De of Liang and De's cousin's son Sheng and Qing Pu of Pei—hence there were the Great Dai, Lesser Dai, and Qing schools, all three established.
translations.idiomatic: Cang taught Dai De of Liang and De's cousin's son Sheng and Qing Pu of Pei—hence there were the Great Dai, Lesser Dai, and Qing schools, all three established.

sentences.zh: 後漢唯曹元傳慶氏，以授其子褒。

translations.literal: In Later Han only Cao Yuan transmitted the Qing school and taught his son Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han only Cao Yuan transmitted the Qing school and taught his son Bao.

sentences.zh: 然三家雖存並微，相傳不絕。

translations.literal: Yet though the three schools survived they were all weak; transmission never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though the three schools survived they were all weak; transmission never ceased.

sentences.zh: 漢末，鄭玄傳小戴之學，後以古經校之，取其于義長者作注，為鄭氏學。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan transmitted the Lesser Dai school, then collated it against the old classic, took what was sound in meaning, and annotated it—this was the Zheng school.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan transmitted the Lesser Dai school, then collated it against the old classic, took what was sound in meaning, and annotated it—this was the Zheng school.

sentences.zh: 其《喪服》一篇，子夏先傳之，諸儒多為注解，今又別行。

translations.literal: 其喪服一篇，子夏先傳之，諸儒多為注解，今又別行。.
translations.idiomatic: 其喪服一篇，子夏先傳之，諸儒多為注解，今又別行。.

sentences.zh: 而漢時有李氏得《周官》。

translations.literal: 而漢時有李氏得周官。.
translations.idiomatic: 而漢時有李氏得周官。.

sentences.zh: 《周官》蓋周公所制官政之法，上于河間獻王，獨闕《冬官》一篇。

translations.literal: 周官蓋周公所制官政之法，上于河間獻王，獨闕冬官一篇。.
translations.idiomatic: 周官蓋周公所制官政之法，上于河間獻王，獨闕冬官一篇。.

sentences.zh: 獻王購以千金不得，遂取《考工記》以補其處，合成六篇奏之。

translations.literal: 獻王購以千金不得，遂取考工記以補其處，合成六篇奏之。.
translations.idiomatic: 獻王購以千金不得，遂取考工記以補其處，合成六篇奏之。.

sentences.zh: 至王莽時，劉歆始置博士，以行於世。

translations.literal: By Wang Mang's time, Liu Xin first established erudites, and it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: By Wang Mang's time, Liu Xin first established erudites, and it circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 河南緱氏及杜子春受業於歆，因以教授。

translations.literal: Goushi of Henan and Du Zichun received instruction from Xin and thus taught others.
translations.idiomatic: Goushi of Henan and Du Zichun received instruction from Xin and thus taught others.

sentences.zh: 是後馬融作《周官傳》，以授鄭玄，玄作《周官注》。

translations.literal: 是後馬融作周官傳，以授鄭玄，玄作周官注。.
translations.idiomatic: 是後馬融作周官傳，以授鄭玄，玄作周官注。.

sentences.zh: 漢初，河間獻王又得仲尼弟子及後學者所記一百三十一篇獻之，時亦無傳之者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, King Xian of Hejian also obtained one hundred thirty-one chapters recorded by Confucius's disciples and later scholars and presented them; at the time there was also no one who transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, King Xian of Hejian also obtained one hundred thirty-one chapters recorded by Confucius's disciples and later scholars and presented them; at the time there was also no one who transmitted them.

sentences.zh: 至劉向考校經籍，檢得一百三十篇，向因第而敘之。

translations.literal: When Liu Xiang collated the classics and records, he found one hundred thirty chapters; Xiang arranged and ordered them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiang collated the classics and records, he found one hundred thirty chapters; Xiang arranged and ordered them.

sentences.zh: 而又得《明堂陰陽記》三十三篇、《孔子三朝記》七篇、《王史氏記》二十一篇、《樂記》二十三篇，凡五種，合二百十四篇。

translations.literal: 而又得明堂陰陽記三十三篇、孔子三朝記七篇、王史氏記二十一篇、Music記二十三篇，凡五種，合二百十四篇。.
translations.idiomatic: 而又得明堂陰陽記三十三篇、孔子三朝記七篇、王史氏記二十一篇、Music記二十三篇，凡五種，合二百十四篇。.

sentences.zh: 戴德刪其煩重，合而記之，為八十五篇，謂之《大戴記》。

translations.literal: 戴德刪其煩重，合而記之，為八十五篇，謂之大戴記。.
translations.idiomatic: 戴德刪其煩重，合而記之，為八十五篇，謂之大戴記。.

sentences.zh: 而戴聖又刪大戴之書，為四十六篇，謂之《小戴記》。

translations.literal: 而戴聖又刪大戴之Documents，為四十六篇，謂之小戴記。.
translations.idiomatic: 而戴聖又刪大戴之Documents，為四十六篇，謂之小戴記。.

sentences.zh: 漢末馬融，遂傳小戴之學。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Ma Rong transmitted the Lesser Dai school.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Ma Rong transmitted the Lesser Dai school.

sentences.zh: 融又定《月令》一篇、《明堂位》一篇、《樂記》一篇，合四十九篇；

translations.literal: 融又定月令一篇、明堂位一篇、Music記一篇，合四十九篇；.
translations.idiomatic: 融又定月令一篇、明堂位一篇、Music記一篇，合四十九篇；.

sentences.zh: 而鄭玄受業於融，又為之注。

translations.idiomatic: 春秋者，魯史策Documents之名。.

sentences.zh: 昔成周微弱，典章淪廢，魯以周公之故，遺制尚存。

translations.literal: In antiquity when Cheng-Zhou was weak and canonical regulations were lost, Lu because of the Duke of Zhou's merit still preserved surviving institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity when Cheng-Zhou was weak and canonical regulations were lost, Lu because of the Duke of Zhou's merit still preserved surviving institutions.

sentences.zh: 仲尼因其舊史，裁而正之，或婉而成章，以存大順，或直書其事，以示首惡。

translations.literal: Confucius, relying on the old histories, trimmed and corrected them—sometimes indirect and forming a pattern to preserve the great order, sometimes writing events directly to show the chief evil.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, relying on the old histories, trimmed and corrected them—sometimes indirect and forming a pattern to preserve the great order, sometimes writing events directly to show the chief evil.

sentences.zh: 故有求名而亡，欲蓋而彰，亂臣賊子，於是大懼。

translations.literal: Hence there are cases of seeking a name yet perishing, wishing to cover yet being exposed—rebellious ministers and wicked sons were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there are cases of seeking a name yet perishing, wishing to cover yet being exposed—rebellious ministers and wicked sons were greatly terrified.

sentences.zh: 其所褒貶，不可具書，皆口授弟子。

translations.literal: What he praised and blamed cannot all be written; all was orally transmitted to disciples.
translations.idiomatic: What he praised and blamed cannot all be written; all was orally transmitted to disciples.

sentences.zh: 弟子退而異說，左丘明恐失其真，乃為之傳。

translations.literal: When disciples withdrew they differed in doctrine; Zuo Qiuming feared the truth would be lost and therefore composed a commentary for it.
translations.idiomatic: When disciples withdrew they differed in doctrine; Zuo Qiuming feared the truth would be lost and therefore composed a commentary for it.

sentences.zh: 遭秦滅學，口說尚存。

translations.literal: When Qin extinguished learning, oral transmission still survived.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin extinguished learning, oral transmission still survived.

sentences.zh: 漢初，有公羊、谷梁、鄒氏、夾氏，四家並行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, the Gongyang, Guliang, Zou, and Jia schools—four in all—were simultaneously current.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, the Gongyang, Guliang, Zou, and Jia schools—four in all—were simultaneously current.

sentences.zh: 王莽之亂，鄒氏無師，夾氏亡。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Wang Mang, the Zou school had no teacher and the Jia school perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Wang Mang, the Zou school had no teacher and the Jia school perished.

sentences.zh: 初，齊人胡母子都傳《公羊春秋》，授東海嬴公。

translations.literal: 初，齊人胡母子都傳公羊春秋，授東海嬴公。.
translations.idiomatic: 初，齊人胡母子都傳公羊春秋，授東海嬴公。.

sentences.zh: 嬴公授東海孟卿，孟卿授魯人眭孟，眭孟授東海嚴彭祖、魯人顏安樂。

translations.literal: Ying Gong taught Meng Qing of Donghai; Meng Qing taught Suimeng of Lu; Suimeng taught Yan Pengzu of Donghai and Yan Anle of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Gong taught Meng Qing of Donghai; Meng Qing taught Suimeng of Lu; Suimeng taught Yan Pengzu of Donghai and Yan Anle of Lu.

sentences.zh: 故後漢《公羊》有嚴氏、顏氏之學，與谷梁三家並立。

translations.literal: 故後漢公羊有嚴氏、顏氏之學，與谷梁三家並立。.
translations.idiomatic: 故後漢公羊有嚴氏、顏氏之學，與谷梁三家並立。.

sentences.zh: 漢末，何休又作《公羊解說》。

translations.literal: 漢末，何休又作公羊解說。.
translations.idiomatic: 漢末，何休又作公羊解說。.

sentences.zh: 而《左氏》漢初出於張蒼之家，本無傳者。

translations.literal: 而左氏漢初出於張蒼之家，本無傳者。.
translations.idiomatic: 而左氏漢初出於張蒼之家，本無傳者。.

sentences.zh: 至文帝時，梁太傅賈誼為訓詁，授趙人貫公。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wen, Grand Tutor Jia Yi of Liang composed exegesis and taught Gong of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Wen, Grand Tutor Jia Yi of Liang composed exegesis and taught Gong of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 其後劉歆典校經籍，考而正之，欲立于學，諸儒莫應。

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Xin supervised collation of classics and records, examined and corrected them, and wished to establish them in the schools, but the Confucian scholars did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Liu Xin supervised collation of classics and records, examined and corrected them, and wished to establish them in the schools, but the Confucian scholars did not respond.

sentences.zh: 至建武中，尚書令韓歆請立而未行。

translations.literal: By the Jianwu era, Director of the Masters of Writing Han Xin requested establishment but it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jianwu era, Director of the Masters of Writing Han Xin requested establishment but it was not carried out.

translations.idiomatic: 時陳元最明左傳，又上Documents訟之。.

translations.idiomatic: 於是乃以魏郡李封為左氏博士。.

sentences.zh: 後群儒蔽固者，數廷爭之。

translations.literal: Afterward obstinate Confucian scholars repeatedly debated it at court.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward obstinate Confucian scholars repeatedly debated it at court.

sentences.zh: 及封卒，遂罷。

translations.literal: When Feng died, it was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng died, it was then abolished.

translations.idiomatic: Afterward Jia Kui and Fu Qian both composed exegesis.

translations.literal: By Wei it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: By Wei it circulated in the world.

translations.idiomatic: 國語Classic of Filial Piety, 1 scroll.

sentences.zh: 右十八部，合六十三卷。

translations.literal: Above: 十八部，合六十三卷.
translations.idiomatic: Above: 十八部，合六十三卷.

translations.idiomatic: Including lost books, totaling 五十九部 titles and 一百一十四卷 scrolls.

sentences.zh: :夫孝者，天之經，地之義，人之行。

translations.literal: Filial piety is Heaven's norm, Earth's righteousness, and human conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is Heaven's norm, Earth's righteousness, and human conduct.

sentences.zh: 自天子達于庶人，雖尊卑有差，及乎行孝，其義一也。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, though honor and humility differ, in the practice of filial piety the meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, though honor and humility differ, in the practice of filial piety the meaning is one.

sentences.zh: 先王因之以治國家，化天下，故能不嚴而順，不肅而成。

translations.literal: The earlier kings relied on it to govern the state, transform All-under-Heaven, and thus could achieve order without severity and completion without austerity.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier kings relied on it to govern the state, transform All-under-Heaven, and thus could achieve order without severity and completion without austerity.

sentences.zh: 斯實生靈之至德，王者之要道。

translations.literal: This is truly the utmost virtue of living beings and the essential Way of kings.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the utmost virtue of living beings and the essential Way of kings.

sentences.zh: 孔子既敘六經，題目不同，指意差別，恐斯道離散，故作《孝經》，以總會之，明其枝流雖分，本萌於孝者也。

translations.literal: 孔子既敘六經，題目不同，指意差別，恐斯道離散，故作孝經，以總會之，明其枝流雖分，本萌於孝者也。.
translations.idiomatic: 孔子既敘六經，題目不同，指意差別，恐斯道離散，故作孝經，以總會之，明其枝流雖分，本萌於孝者也。.

sentences.zh: 遭秦焚書，為河間人顏芝所藏。

translations.literal: When Qin burned books, it was hidden by Yan Zhi of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin burned books, it was hidden by Yan Zhi of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 漢初，芝子貞出之，凡十八章，而長孫氏、博士江翁、少府後蒼、諫議大夫翼奉、安昌侯張禹，皆名其學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Zhi's son Zhen brought it forth—in all eighteen chapters—and the Chief of the Changsun clan, Erudite Jiang Weng, Director of the Palace Workshop Hou Cang, Remonstrance Grandee Ji Feng, and Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang all named their schools after it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Zhi's son Zhen brought it forth—in all eighteen chapters—and the Chief of the Changsun clan, Erudite Jiang Weng, Director of the Palace Workshop Hou Cang, Remonstrance Grandee Ji Feng, and Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang all named their schools after it.

sentences.zh: 又有《古文孝經》，與《古文尚書》同出，而長孫有《閨門》一章，其餘經文，大較相似，篇簡缺解，又有衍出三章，並前合為二十二章，孔安國為之傳。

translations.literal: There was also 古文Classic of Filial Piety, transmitted by 與《古文尚書》同出，而長孫有《閨門》一章，其餘經文，大較相似，篇簡缺解，又有衍出三章，並前合為二十二章，孔安國為之.
translations.idiomatic: There was also 古文Classic of Filial Piety, transmitted by 與《古文尚書》同出，而長孫有《閨門》一章，其餘經文，大較相似，篇簡缺解，又有衍出三章，並前合為二十二章，孔安國為之.

sentences.zh: 至劉向典校經籍，以顏本比古文，除其繁惑，以十八章為定。

translations.literal: When Liu Xiang supervised collation of classics and records, he compared Yan's text against the ancient script, removed what was redundant and confusing, and fixed it at eighteen chapters.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiang supervised collation of classics and records, he compared Yan's text against the ancient script, removed what was redundant and confusing, and fixed it at eighteen chapters.

sentences.zh: 鄭眾、馬融，並為之注。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong and Ma Rong both annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong and Ma Rong both annotated it.

sentences.zh: 又有鄭氏注，相傳或雲鄭玄，其立義與玄所注餘書不同，故疑之。

translations.literal: There is also a Zheng commentary, transmitted as being by Zheng Xuan; its established meaning differs from Xuan's annotations on his other books, hence it is doubted.
translations.idiomatic: There is also a Zheng commentary, transmitted as being by Zheng Xuan; its established meaning differs from Xuan's annotations on his other books, hence it is doubted.

sentences.zh: 梁代，安國及鄭氏二家，並立國學，而安國之本，亡于梁亂。

translations.literal: In the Liang dynasty the Anguo and Zheng schools were both listed in the National University, but Anguo's text was lost in the turmoil of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liang dynasty the Anguo and Zheng schools were both listed in the National University, but Anguo's text was lost in the turmoil of Liang.

sentences.zh: 陳及周、齊，唯傳鄭氏。

translations.literal: In Chen and under Zhou and Qi, only the Zheng school was transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen and under Zhou and Qi, only the Zheng school was transmitted.

sentences.zh: 至隋，秘書監王劭于京師訪得《孔傳》，送至河間劉炫。

translations.literal: 至隋，秘Documents監王劭于京師訪得孔傳，送至河間劉炫。.
translations.idiomatic: 至隋，秘Documents監王劭于京師訪得孔傳，送至河間劉炫。.

sentences.zh: 炫因序其得喪，述其議疏，講於人間，漸聞朝廷，後遂著令，與鄭氏並立。

translations.literal: Xuan ordered its gains and losses, set forth its discussions and subcommentary, and lectured among the people; it gradually reached the court, and afterward an edict was issued establishing it alongside the Zheng school.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan ordered its gains and losses, set forth its discussions and subcommentary, and lectured among the people; it gradually reached the court, and afterward an edict was issued establishing it alongside the Zheng school.

sentences.zh: 儒者喧喧，皆雲炫自作之，非孔舊本，而秘府又先無其書。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars clamored, all saying Xuan had composed it himself and that it was not Confucius's old text; moreover the secret repository had never had the book.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars clamored, all saying Xuan had composed it himself and that it was not Confucius's old text; moreover the secret repository had never had the book.

sentences.zh: 又雲魏氏遷洛，未達華語，孝文帝命侯伏侯可悉陵，以夷言譯《孝經》之旨，教於國人，謂之《國語孝經》。

sentences.zh: 孔子既敘六經，講於洙、泗之上，門徒三千，達者七十。

translations.literal: After Confucius had arranged the Six Classics and lectured on the banks of the Zhu and Si, he had three thousand disciples, seventy of whom mastered the Way.
translations.idiomatic: After Confucius had arranged the Six Classics and lectured on the banks of the Zhu and Si, he had three thousand disciples, seventy of whom mastered the Way.

sentences.zh: 其與夫子應答，及私相講肄，言合於道，或書之於紳，或事之無厭。

translations.literal: Their responses to the Master and their private discussions and studies—words in accord with the Way—were sometimes written on their sashes and sometimes pursued without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Their responses to the Master and their private discussions and studies—words in accord with the Way—were sometimes written on their sashes and sometimes pursued without satiety.

sentences.zh: 仲尼既沒，遂緝而論之，謂之《論語》。

translations.literal: 仲尼既沒，遂緝而論之，謂之論語。.
translations.idiomatic: 仲尼既沒，遂緝而論之，謂之論語。.

sentences.zh: 漢初，有齊、魯之說。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han there were Qi and Lu versions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han there were Qi and Lu versions.

sentences.zh: 其齊人傳者二十二篇，魯人傳者二十篇。

translations.literal: Those transmitted in Qi had twenty-two chapters; those in Lu had twenty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Those transmitted in Qi had twenty-two chapters; those in Lu had twenty chapters.

sentences.zh: 齊則昌邑中尉王吉、少府宗畸、御史大夫貢禹、尚書令五鹿充宗、膠東庸生。

translations.literal: In Qi: Wang Ji, Commandant of Changyi; Zong Qi, Director of the Palace Workshop; Gong Yu, Grand Secretary; Wulu Chongzong, Director of the Masters of Writing; Yong Sheng of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi: Wang Ji, Commandant of Changyi; Zong Qi, Director of the Palace Workshop; Gong Yu, Grand Secretary; Wulu Chongzong, Director of the Masters of Writing; Yong Sheng of Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: 魯則常山都尉龔奮、長信少府夏侯勝、韋丞相節侯父子、魯扶卿、前將軍蕭望之、安昌侯張禹，並名其學。

translations.literal: In Lu: Gong Fen, Commandant of Changshan; Xiahou Sheng, Director of the Palace Workshop of Changxin; Lord Wei, Marquis of Jie, father and son; Fu Qing of Lu; Xiao Wangzhi, Former General of the Vanguard; Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang—all named their schools after it.
translations.idiomatic: In Lu: Gong Fen, Commandant of Changshan; Xiahou Sheng, Director of the Palace Workshop of Changxin; Lord Wei, Marquis of Jie, father and son; Fu Qing of Lu; Xiao Wangzhi, Former General of the Vanguard; Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang—all named their schools after it.

sentences.zh: 張禹本授《魯論》，晚講《齊論》，後遂合而考之，刪其煩惑。

translations.literal: 張禹本授魯論，晚講齊論，後遂合而考之，刪其煩惑。.
translations.idiomatic: 張禹本授魯論，晚講齊論，後遂合而考之，刪其煩惑。.

sentences.zh: 除去《齊論·問王》、《知道》二篇，從《魯論》二十篇為定，號《張侯論》，當世重之。

translations.literal: 除去齊論·問王、知道二篇，從魯論二十篇為定，號張侯論，當世重之。.
translations.idiomatic: 除去齊論·問王、知道二篇，從魯論二十篇為定，號張侯論，當世重之。.

sentences.zh: 周氏、包氏為之章句，馬融又為之訓。

translations.literal: The Zhou and Bao clans composed commentarial glosses; Ma Rong also composed exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou and Bao clans composed commentarial glosses; Ma Rong also composed exegesis.

sentences.zh: 又有古《論語》，與《古文尚書》同出，章句煩省，與《魯論》不異，唯分《子張》為二篇，故有二十一篇。

translations.literal: 又有古論語，與Old Text Documents同出，章句煩省，與魯論不異，唯分子張為二篇，故有二十一篇。.
translations.idiomatic: 又有古論語，與Old Text Documents同出，章句煩省，與魯論不異，唯分子張為二篇，故有二十一篇。.

sentences.zh: 孔安國為之傳。

translations.literal: Kong Anguo composed a tradition for it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo composed a tradition for it.

sentences.zh: 漢末，鄭玄以《張侯論》為本，參考《齊論》、古《論》而為之注。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan took the Marquis Zhang's Discourses as his base, consulted the Qi Discourses and the Old Discourses, and annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan took the Marquis Zhang's Discourses as his base, consulted the Qi Discourses and the Old Discourses, and annotated the Analects.

sentences.zh: 魏司空陳群、太常王肅、博士周生烈，皆為義說。

translations.literal: Chen Qun, Minister of Works of Wei, Wang Su, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Erudite Zhou Shengli all composed explications of meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun, Minister of Works of Wei, Wang Su, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Erudite Zhou Shengli all composed explications of meaning.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書何晏又為集解。

translations.literal: He Yan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, also composed collected explanations.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, also composed collected explanations.

sentences.zh: 是後諸儒多為之注，《齊論》遂亡。

translations.literal: 是後諸儒多為之注，齊論遂亡。.
translations.idiomatic: 是後諸儒多為之注，齊論遂亡。.

sentences.zh: 古《論》先無師說，梁、陳之時，唯鄭玄、何晏立于國學，而鄭氏甚微。

translations.literal: 古論先無師說，梁、陳之時，唯鄭玄、何晏立于國學，而鄭氏甚微。.
translations.idiomatic: 古論先無師說，梁、陳之時，唯鄭玄、何晏立于國學，而鄭氏甚微。.

sentences.zh: 周、齊，鄭學獨立。

translations.literal: Under Zhou and Qi, the Zheng school alone was established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou and Qi, the Zheng school alone was established.

sentences.zh: 至隋，何、鄭並行，鄭氏盛於人間。

translations.literal: By Sui, He and Zheng were both current; the Zheng school flourished among the people.
translations.idiomatic: By Sui, He and Zheng were both current; the Zheng school flourished among the people.

sentences.zh: 其《孔叢》、《家語》，並孔氏所傳仲尼之旨。

translations.literal: 其孔叢、家語，並孔氏所傳仲尼之旨。.
translations.idiomatic: 其孔叢、家語，並孔氏所傳仲尼之旨。.

sentences.zh: 《爾雅》諸書，解古今之意，並五經總義，附於此篇。

translations.literal: 爾雅諸Documents，解古今之意，並五經總義，附於此篇。.
translations.idiomatic: 爾雅諸Documents，解古今之意，並五經總義，附於此篇。.

sentences.zh: 經緯《河圖》二十卷梁《河圖洛書》二十四卷，目錄一卷，亡。

translations.literal: 經緯河圖二十卷梁河圖洛Documents二十四卷，目錄一卷，亡。.
translations.idiomatic: 經緯河圖二十卷梁河圖洛Documents二十四卷，目錄一卷，亡。.

translations.idiomatic: 河圖龍文, 1 scroll.

translations.idiomatic: Documents緯, 3 scrolls, 鄭玄注，梁六卷.

translations.idiomatic: Intermediate Annals of the Documents, 5 scrolls, annotated by 鄭玄.

sentences.zh: 梁有八卷，今殘缺。

translations.literal: The Liang catalog had 8 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed 8 scrolls.

translations.literal: Classic: Odes緯, 18 scrolls, Wei Erudite annotated by 宋均.
translations.idiomatic: Classic: Odes緯, 18 scrolls, Wei Erudite annotated by 宋均.

sentences.zh: 梁十卷。

translations.literal: The Liang catalog had ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed ten scrolls.

translations.literal: Rites緯, 3 scrolls, annotated by 鄭玄, lost.
translations.idiomatic: Rites緯, 3 scrolls, annotated by 鄭玄, lost.

translations.literal: Record of Rites默房, 2 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.
translations.idiomatic: Record of Rites默房, 2 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.

sentences.zh: 梁有三卷，鄭玄注，亡。

translations.literal: The Liang catalog had 3 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed 3 scrolls.

translations.literal: Music緯, 3 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.
translations.idiomatic: Music緯, 3 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.

sentences.zh: 梁有《樂五鳥圖》一卷。

translations.literal: The Liang catalog had music五鳥圖, 1 scroll.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed music五鳥圖, 1 scroll.

sentences.zh: 亡。

translations.literal: Lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lost.

sentences.zh: 《春秋災異》十五卷郗萌撰。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn災異, 15 scrolls, composed by 郗萌.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn災異, 15 scrolls, composed by 郗萌.

sentences.zh: 梁有《春秋緯》三十卷，宋均注；

translations.literal: The Liang catalog had Spring and Autumn緯, 30 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed Spring and Autumn緯, 30 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.

sentences.zh: 《春秋內事》四卷，《春秋包命》二卷，《春秋秘事》十一卷，《書、易、詩、孝經、春秋、河洛緯秘要》一卷，《五帝鉤命訣圖》一卷。

translations.literal: 春秋內事四卷，春秋包命二卷，春秋秘事十一卷，Documents、易、Odes、孝經、春秋、河洛緯秘要一卷，五帝鉤命訣圖一卷。.
translations.idiomatic: 春秋內事四卷，春秋包命二卷，春秋秘事十一卷，Documents、易、Odes、孝經、春秋、河洛緯秘要一卷，五帝鉤命訣圖一卷。.

sentences.zh: 亡。

translations.literal: Lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lost.

translations.literal: Classic of Filial Piety勾命訣, 6 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of Filial Piety勾命訣, 6 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.

translations.literal: Classic of Filial Piety援神契, 7 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of Filial Piety援神契, 7 scrolls, Song annotated by 均.

translations.literal: Classic of Filial Piety內事, 1 scroll, Liang annotated by 有《孝經雜緯》十卷，宋均.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of Filial Piety內事, 1 scroll, Liang annotated by 有《孝經雜緯》十卷，宋均.

sentences.zh: 《孝經元命包》一卷，《孝經古秘援神》二卷，《孝經古秘圖》一卷，《孝經左右握》二卷，《孝經左右契圖》一卷，《孝經雌雄圖》三卷，《孝經異本雌雄圖》二卷，《孝經分野圖》一卷，《孝經內事圖》二卷，《孝經內事星宿講堂七十二弟子圖》一卷，又《口授圖》一卷；

translations.literal: 孝經元命包一卷，孝經古秘援神二卷，孝經古秘圖一卷，孝經左右握二卷，孝經左右契圖一卷，孝經雌雄圖三卷，孝經異本雌雄圖二卷，孝經分野圖一卷，孝經內事圖二卷，孝經內事星宿講堂七十二弟子圖一卷，又口授圖一卷；.
translations.idiomatic: 孝經元命包一卷，孝經古秘援神二卷，孝經古秘圖一卷，孝經左右握二卷，孝經左右契圖一卷，孝經雌雄圖三卷，孝經異本雌雄圖二卷，孝經分野圖一卷，孝經內事圖二卷，孝經內事星宿講堂七十二弟子圖一卷，又口授圖一卷；.

sentences.zh: 又《論語讖》八卷，宋均注；

translations.literal: 又論語讖八卷，宋均注；.
translations.idiomatic: 又論語讖八卷，宋均注；.

sentences.zh: 《孔老讖》十二卷，《老子河洛讖》一卷，《尹公讖》四卷，《劉向讖》一卷，《雜讖書》二十九卷，《堯戒舜、禹》一卷，《孔子王明鏡》一卷，《郭文金雄記》一卷，《王子年歌》一卷，《嵩高道士歌》一卷。

translations.literal: 孔老讖十二卷，老子河洛讖一卷，尹公讖四卷，劉向讖一卷，雜讖Documents二十九卷，堯戒舜、禹一卷，孔子王明鏡一卷，郭文金雄記一卷，王子年歌一卷，嵩高道士歌一卷。.
translations.idiomatic: 孔老讖十二卷，老子河洛讖一卷，尹公讖四卷，劉向讖一卷，雜讖Documents二十九卷，堯戒舜、禹一卷，孔子王明鏡一卷，郭文金雄記一卷，王子年歌一卷，嵩高道士歌一卷。.

sentences.zh: 亡。

translations.literal: Lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lost.

sentences.zh: 右十三部，合九十二卷。

translations.literal: Above: 十三部，合九十二卷.
translations.idiomatic: Above: 十三部，合九十二卷.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合三十二部，共二百三十二卷。

translations.literal: Counting lost books together, 三十二部 titles, 共二百三十二卷 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Including lost books, totaling 三十二部 titles and 共二百三十二卷 scrolls.

sentences.zh: :《易》曰：「河出圖，洛出書。

translations.literal: 易曰：「河出圖，洛出Documents。.
translations.idiomatic: 易曰：「河出圖，洛出Documents。.

sentences.zh: 」然則聖人之受命也，必因積德累業，豐功厚利，誠著天地，澤被生人，萬物之所歸往，神明之所福饗，則有天命之應。

translations.literal: Thus when the sage receives the Mandate, he must build on accumulated virtue and repeated achievement, abundant merit and thick benefit, sincerity manifest to Heaven and Earth and grace covering the living—what the myriad things turn toward and what the spirits bless—then there is a response of the Heavenly Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the sage receives the Mandate, he must build on accumulated virtue and repeated achievement, abundant merit and thick benefit, sincerity manifest to Heaven and Earth and grace covering the living—what the myriad things turn toward and what the spirits bless—then there is a response of the Heavenly Mandate.

sentences.zh: 蓋龜龍銜負，出於河、洛，以紀易代之徵，其理幽昧，究極神道。

translations.literal: Tortoises and dragons bear and carry them, emerging from the River and Luo, to record signs of dynastic change; the principle is obscure and reaches to the spirit-way.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoises and dragons bear and carry them, emerging from the River and Luo, to record signs of dynastic change; the principle is obscure and reaches to the spirit-way.

sentences.zh: 先王恐其惑人，秘而不傳。

translations.literal: The earlier kings feared they would confuse people and kept them secret without transmitting them.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier kings feared they would confuse people and kept them secret without transmitting them.

sentences.zh: 說者又雲，孔子既敘六經，以明天人之道，知後世不能稽同其意，故別立緯及讖，以遺來世。

translations.literal: Expositors also say that after Confucius had arranged the Six Classics to clarify the Way of Heaven and man, knowing later generations could not examine together his intent, he separately established weft texts and prognostications to leave them to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors also say that after Confucius had arranged the Six Classics to clarify the Way of Heaven and man, knowing later generations could not examine together his intent, he separately established weft texts and prognostications to leave them to posterity.

sentences.zh: 其書出於前漢，有《河圖》九篇，《洛書》六篇，雲自黃帝至周文王所受本文。

translations.literal: 其Documents出於前漢，有河圖九篇，洛Documents六篇，雲自黃帝至周文王所受本文。.
translations.idiomatic: 其Documents出於前漢，有河圖九篇，洛Documents六篇，雲自黃帝至周文王所受本文。.

sentences.zh: 又別有三十篇，雲自初起至於孔子，九聖之所增演，以廣其意。

translations.literal: There are also thirty chapters, said to have been expanded by the nine sages from the beginning down to Confucius to broaden the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: There are also thirty chapters, said to have been expanded by the nine sages from the beginning down to Confucius to broaden the meaning.

sentences.zh: 又有《七經緯》三十六篇，並雲孔子所作，並前合為八十一篇。

translations.literal: There was also 七經緯, 三十六篇，並雲孔子所作，並前合為八十一篇.
translations.idiomatic: There was also 七經緯, 三十六篇，並雲孔子所作，並前合為八十一篇.

sentences.zh: 而又有《尚書中候》、《洛罪級》、《五行傳》、《詩推度災》、《氾曆樞》、《含神務》、《孝經勾命訣》、《援神契》、《雜讖》等書。

translations.literal: 而又有Documents中候、洛罪級、五行傳、Odes推度災、氾曆樞、含神務、孝經勾命訣、援神契、雜讖等Documents。.
translations.idiomatic: 而又有Documents中候、洛罪級、五行傳、Odes推度災、氾曆樞、含神務、孝經勾命訣、援神契、雜讖等Documents。.

sentences.zh: 漢代有郗氏、袁氏說。

translations.literal: In Han there were the Xi and Yuan schools of exposition.
translations.idiomatic: In Han there were the Xi and Yuan schools of exposition.

sentences.zh: 漢末，郎中郗萌集圖緯讖雜占為五十篇，謂之《春秋災異》。

translations.literal: 漢末，郎中郗萌集圖緯讖雜占為五十篇，謂之春秋災異。.
translations.idiomatic: 漢末，郎中郗萌集圖緯讖雜占為五十篇，謂之春秋災異。.

sentences.zh: 宋均、鄭玄並為讖律之注。

translations.literal: Song Jun and Zheng Xuan both composed annotations on prognostications and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jun and Zheng Xuan both composed annotations on prognostications and statutes.

sentences.zh: 然其文辭淺俗，顛倒舛謬，不類聖人之旨。

translations.literal: Yet their literary phrasing is shallow and vulgar, inverted and erroneous, not resembling the purport of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their literary phrasing is shallow and vulgar, inverted and erroneous, not resembling the purport of the sages.

sentences.zh: 相傳疑世人造為之後，或者又加點竄，非其實錄。

translations.literal: Transmission suggests that after people of the world fabricated them, some perhaps further altered them—it is not a true record.
translations.idiomatic: Transmission suggests that after people of the world fabricated them, some perhaps further altered them—it is not a true record.

sentences.zh: 起王莽好符命，光武以圖讖興，遂盛行於世。

translations.literal: It began when Wang Mang loved token-destiny; Emperor Guangwu rose through charts and prognostications, and thus it greatly flourished in the world.
translations.idiomatic: It began when Wang Mang loved token-destiny; Emperor Guangwu rose through charts and prognostications, and thus it greatly flourished in the world.

sentences.zh: 漢時，又詔東平王蒼正五經章句，皆命從讖。

translations.literal: In Han an edict also ordered King Cang of Dongping to correct the commentarial glosses of the Five Classics—all were commanded to follow prognostications.
translations.idiomatic: In Han an edict also ordered King Cang of Dongping to correct the commentarial glosses of the Five Classics—all were commanded to follow prognostications.

sentences.zh: 俗儒趨時，益為其學，篇卷第目，轉加增廣。

translations.literal: Vulgar Confucians chased the times and further made it their learning; scrolls and titles grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Vulgar Confucians chased the times and further made it their learning; scrolls and titles grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 言五經者，皆憑讖為說。

translations.literal: Those who spoke of the Five Classics all relied on prognostications as their explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who spoke of the Five Classics all relied on prognostications as their explanation.

sentences.zh: 唯孔安國、毛公、王璜、賈逵之徒獨非之，相承以為妖妄，亂中庸之典。

translations.literal: Only Kong Anguo, Lord Mao, Wang Huang, Jia Kui, and the like rejected it, transmitting the view that it was delusive and false, disordering the canonical mean.
translations.idiomatic: Only Kong Anguo, Lord Mao, Wang Huang, Jia Kui, and the like rejected it, transmitting the view that it was delusive and false, disordering the canonical mean.

sentences.zh: 故因漢魯恭王、河間獻王所得古文，參而考之，以成其義，謂之「古學」。

translations.literal: Therefore, relying on the ancient script obtained by King Gong of Lu and King Xian of Hejian in Han, they collated and examined it to complete its meaning—this was called "ancient learning."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, relying on the ancient script obtained by King Gong of Lu and King Xian of Hejian in Han, they collated and examined it to complete its meaning—this was called "ancient learning."

sentences.zh: 當世之儒，又非毀之，竟不得行。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars of the age also denounced and destroyed it; in the end it could not be established.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars of the age also denounced and destroyed it; in the end it could not be established.

sentences.zh: 魏代王肅，推引古學，以難其義。

translations.literal: Wang Su of Wei promoted ancient learning to challenge its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su of Wei promoted ancient learning to challenge its meaning.

sentences.zh: 王弼、杜預，從而明之，自是古學稍立。

translations.literal: Wang Bi and Du Yu followed and clarified it; from this ancient learning was gradually established.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi and Du Yu followed and clarified it; from this ancient learning was gradually established.

sentences.zh: 至宋大明中，始禁圖讖，梁天監已後，又重其制。

translations.literal: By the Daming era of Song, charts and prognostications were first banned; after the Tianjian era of Liang the prohibition was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: By the Daming era of Song, charts and prognostications were first banned; after the Tianjian era of Liang the prohibition was renewed.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，禁之逾切。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, the ban was even stricter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, the ban was even stricter.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，乃發使四出，搜天下書籍與讖緯相涉者，皆焚之，為吏所糾者至死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he sent emissaries in four directions to search books throughout the realm; whatever was connected with prognostications and weft texts was burned; those reported by officials were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he sent emissaries in four directions to search books throughout the realm; whatever was connected with prognostications and weft texts was burned; those reported by officials were punished by death.

sentences.zh: 自是無複其學，秘府之內，亦多散亡。

translations.literal: From this the learning no longer existed; within the secret repository much was also lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: From this the learning no longer existed; within the secret repository much was also lost and scattered.

sentences.zh: 今錄其見存，列於六經之下，以備異說。

translations.literal: Now what survives in writing is recorded and listed under the Six Classics to preserve variant doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Now what survives in writing is recorded and listed under the Six Classics to preserve variant doctrines.

sentences.zh: :孔子曰：「必也正名乎！

translations.literal: Confucius said: "One must rectify names!"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "One must rectify names!"

sentences.zh: 」名謂書字。

translations.literal: Names mean written characters.
translations.idiomatic: Names mean written characters.

sentences.zh: 「名不正則言不順，言不順則事不成。

translations.literal: If names are not correct, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: If names are not correct, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not accomplished.

sentences.zh: 」說者以為書之所起，起自黃帝蒼頡。

translations.literal: Expositors hold that writing arose from Yellow Emperor's Cang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors hold that writing arose from Yellow Emperor's Cang Jie.

sentences.zh: 比類象形謂之文，形聲相益謂之字，著於竹帛謂之書。

translations.literal: Comparing categories and picturing forms is called wen; form and sound mutually enhancing is called zi; written on bamboo and silk is called shu.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing categories and picturing forms is called wen; form and sound mutually enhancing is called zi; written on bamboo and silk is called shu.

sentences.zh: 故有象形、諧聲、會意、轉注、假借、處事六義之別。

translations.literal: Hence there are the six categories: pictographs, phonetic compounds, combined meanings, explanatory transference, loan characters, and indicative forms.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there are the six categories: pictographs, phonetic compounds, combined meanings, explanatory transference, loan characters, and indicative forms.

sentences.zh: 古者童子示而不誑，六年教之數與方名。

translations.literal: In antiquity boys were shown things without deception; at six they were taught numbers and directional names.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity boys were shown things without deception; at six they were taught numbers and directional names.

sentences.zh: 十歲入小學，學書計。

translations.literal: At ten they entered elementary school and learned writing and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: At ten they entered elementary school and learned writing and calculation.

sentences.zh: 二十而冠，始習先王之道，故能成其德而任事。

translations.literal: At twenty they capped and began to study the Way of the earlier kings, and thus could complete their virtue and undertake affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty they capped and began to study the Way of the earlier kings, and thus could complete their virtue and undertake affairs.

sentences.zh: 然自蒼頡訖于漢初，書經五變：一曰古文，即蒼頡所作。

translations.literal: Yet from Cang Jie down to the beginning of Han, writing underwent five changes: first, ancient script, what Cang Jie created.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Cang Jie down to the beginning of Han, writing underwent five changes: first, ancient script, what Cang Jie created.

sentences.zh: 二曰大篆，周宣王時史籀所作。

translations.literal: Second, large seal script, what Scribe Zhou created in the time of King Xuan of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Second, large seal script, what Scribe Zhou created in the time of King Xuan of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 三曰小篆，秦時李斯所作。

translations.literal: Third, small seal script, what Li Si created in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Third, small seal script, what Li Si created in Qin.

sentences.zh: 四曰隸書，程邈所作。

translations.literal: Fourth, clerical script, what Cheng Miao created.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, clerical script, what Cheng Miao created.

sentences.zh: 五曰草書，漢初作。

translations.literal: Fifth, cursive script, created at the beginning of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, cursive script, created at the beginning of Han.

sentences.zh: 秦世既廢古文，始用八體，有大篆、小篆、刻符、摹印、蟲書、署書、殳書、隸書。

translations.literal: When Qin abolished ancient script it first used eight styles: large seal, small seal, carved tally, seal impression, insect script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin abolished ancient script it first used eight styles: large seal, small seal, carved tally, seal impression, insect script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 漢時以六體教學童，有古文、奇字、篆書、隸書、繆篆、蟲鳥，並槁書、楷書、懸針、垂露、飛白等二十餘種之勢，皆出於上六書，因事生變也。

translations.literal: In Han the six styles were used to teach schoolboys: ancient script, odd characters, seal script, clerical script, twisted seal, and bird-and-insect—together with draft script, regular script, suspended needle, hanging dew, flying white, and more than twenty forms, all arising from the six scripts above and changing according to circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: In Han the six styles were used to teach schoolboys: ancient script, odd characters, seal script, clerical script, twisted seal, and bird-and-insect—together with draft script, regular script, suspended needle, hanging dew, flying white, and more than twenty forms, all arising from the six scripts above and changing according to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 魏世又有八分書，其字義訓讀，有《史籀篇》、《蒼頡篇》、《三蒼》、《埤蒼》、《廣蒼》等諸篇章，訓詁、《說文》《字林》、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸書。

translations.literal: 魏世又有八分Documents，其字義訓讀，有史籀篇、蒼頡篇、三蒼、埤蒼、廣蒼等諸篇章，訓詁、說文字林、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸Documents。.
translations.idiomatic: 魏世又有八分Documents，其字義訓讀，有史籀篇、蒼頡篇、三蒼、埤蒼、廣蒼等諸篇章，訓詁、說文字林、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸Documents。.

sentences.zh: 自後漢佛法行於中國，又得西域胡書，能以十四字貫一切音，文省而義廣，謂之婆羅門書，與八體六文之義殊別，今取以附體勢之下。

translations.literal: Afterward in Later Han Buddhist teaching spread in China and Western Region Kharosthi script was also obtained, able to cover all sounds with fourteen letters—text economical and meaning broad—called Brahmin script; its principle differs from the eight styles and six scripts, and is now appended under forms and styles.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward in Later Han Buddhist teaching spread in China and Western Region Kharosthi script was also obtained, able to cover all sounds with fourteen letters—text economical and meaning broad—called Brahmin script; its principle differs from the eight styles and six scripts, and is now appended under forms and styles.

sentences.zh: 又後魏初定中原，軍容號令，皆經夷語，後染華俗，多不能通，故錄其本言，相傳教習，謂之「國語」，今取以附音韻之末。

translations.literal: Also when Later Wei first settled the Central Plains, military commands were all in barbarian speech; afterward influenced by Chinese custom, many could not be understood, so the original words were recorded and transmitted for teaching—called the "National Language"—now appended at the end of phonology.
translations.idiomatic: Also when Later Wei first settled the Central Plains, military commands were all in barbarian speech; afterward influenced by Chinese custom, many could not be understood, so the original words were recorded and transmitted for teaching—called the "National Language"—now appended at the end of phonology.

sentences.zh: 又後漢鐫刻七經，著於石碑，皆蔡邕所書。

translations.literal: Also in Later Han the Seven Classics were carved on stone tablets, all written by Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Later Han the Seven Classics were carved on stone tablets, all written by Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 魏正始中，又立三字石經，相承以為七經正字。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei a three-script stone classic was also established; by transmission it was considered the correct characters of the Seven Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era of Wei a three-script stone classic was also established; by transmission it was considered the correct characters of the Seven Classics.

sentences.zh: 後魏之末，齊神武執政，自洛陽徙於鄴都，行至河陽，值岸崩，遂沒于水。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Wei, when Qi Emperor Shenwu held power, they were moved from Luoyang to the capital at Ye; passing Heyang, the bank collapsed and they sank in the water.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Wei, when Qi Emperor Shenwu held power, they were moved from Luoyang to the capital at Ye; passing Heyang, the bank collapsed and they sank in the water.

sentences.zh: 其得至鄴者，不盈太半。

translations.literal: Of what reached Ye, not even half remained.
translations.idiomatic: Of what reached Ye, not even half remained.

sentences.zh: 至隋開皇六年，又自鄴京載入長安，置於秘書內省，議欲補緝，立于國學。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang of Sui they were again carried from the capital at Ye into Chang'an and placed in the inner secretariat; it was proposed to repair and compile them and establish them in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaihuang of Sui they were again carried from the capital at Ye into Chang'an and placed in the inner secretariat; it was proposed to repair and compile them and establish them in the National University.

sentences.zh: 尋屬隋亂，事遂寢廢，營造之司，因用為柱礎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Sui fell into disorder and the matter was abandoned; the construction office used them as pillar bases.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sui fell into disorder and the matter was abandoned; the construction office used them as pillar bases.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，秘書監臣魏徵，始收聚之，十不存一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Minister of the Secretariat Wei Zheng first gathered them together—not one in ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Minister of the Secretariat Wei Zheng first gathered them together—not one in ten survived.

sentences.zh: 其相承傳拓之本，猶在秘府，並秦帝刻石，附於此篇，以備小學。

translations.literal: Rubbing copies transmitted by inheritance still remain in the secret repository, together with the Qin emperor's carved stones, appended to this section to complete elementary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Rubbing copies transmitted by inheritance still remain in the secret repository, together with the Qin emperor's carved stones, appended to this section to complete elementary learning.

sentences.zh: 凡六藝經緯六百二十七部，五千三百七十一卷。

translations.literal: In all, the Six Arts classics and weft texts: six hundred twenty-seven titles, five thousand three hundred seventy-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the Six Arts classics and weft texts: six hundred twenty-seven titles, five thousand three hundred seventy-one scrolls.

sentences.zh: 通計亡書，合九百五十部，七千二百九十卷。

translations.literal: Counting lost books together, 九百五十部 titles, 七千二百九十卷 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Including lost books, totaling 九百五十部 titles and 七千二百九十卷 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 【結】《傳》曰：「玉不琢，不成器；

translations.literal: 【結】傳曰：「玉不琢，不成器；.
translations.idiomatic: 【結】傳曰：「玉不琢，不成器；.

sentences.zh: 人不學，不知道。

translations.literal: If people do not study, they do not know the Way.
translations.idiomatic: If people do not study, they do not know the Way.

sentences.zh: 」古之君子，多識而不窮，畜疑以待問：學不逾等，教不陵節；

translations.literal: The gentlemen of antiquity were broadly learned without exhaustion, storing doubts to await questioning: learning did not overstep rank, teaching did not cross gradation;
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of antiquity were broadly learned without exhaustion, storing doubts to await questioning: learning did not overstep rank, teaching did not cross gradation;

sentences.zh: 言約而易曉，師逸而功倍；

translations.literal: words were concise and easy to understand, the teacher at ease and achievement doubled;
translations.idiomatic: words were concise and easy to understand, the teacher at ease and achievement doubled;

sentences.zh: 且耕且養，三年而成一藝。

translations.literal: they both plowed and nurtured, and in three years completed one art.
translations.idiomatic: they both plowed and nurtured, and in three years completed one art.

sentences.zh: 自孔子沒而微言絕，七十子喪而大義乖，學者離群索居，各為異說。

translations.literal: From the time Confucius died and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples passed away and the great meaning went astray; scholars lived apart in isolation, each forming a different doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Confucius died and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples passed away and the great meaning went astray. Scholars lived apart in isolation, each forming a different doctrine.

sentences.zh: 至於戰國，典文遺棄，六經之儒，不能究其宗旨，多立小數，一經至數百萬言。

translations.literal: Down to the Warring States, canonical texts were abandoned; Confucian scholars of the Six Classics could not exhaust their fundamental purport and mostly established minor techniques—a single classic reaching millions of words.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Warring States, canonical texts were abandoned; Confucian scholars of the Six Classics could not exhaust their fundamental purport and mostly established minor techniques—a single classic reaching millions of words.

sentences.zh: 致令學者難曉，虛誦問答，脣腐齒落而不知益。

translations.literal: This caused scholars difficulty in understanding; they recited emptily in question and answer until lips rotted and teeth fell out without knowing benefit.
translations.idiomatic: This caused scholars difficulty in understanding; they recited emptily in question and answer until lips rotted and teeth fell out without knowing benefit.

sentences.zh: 且先王設教，以防人欲，必本於人事，折之中道。

translations.literal: The earlier kings established teaching to guard against human desire; it must be rooted in human affairs and broken at the mean.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier kings established teaching to guard against human desire; it must be rooted in human affairs and broken at the mean.

sentences.zh: 上天之命，略而罕言，方外之理，固所未說。

translations.literal: Heaven's command is brief and rarely spoken; principles outside the square were indeed not yet explained.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's command is brief and rarely spoken; principles outside the square were indeed not yet explained.

sentences.zh: 至後漢好圖讖，晉世重玄言，穿鑿妄作，日以滋生。

translations.literal: By Later Han charts and prognostications were favored; in the Jin era abstruse talk was honored—boring through and fabricating, daily multiplying.
translations.idiomatic: By Later Han charts and prognostications were favored; in the Jin era abstruse talk was honored—boring through and fabricating, daily multiplying.

sentences.zh: 先王正典，雜之以妖妄，大雅之論，汨之以放誕。

translations.literal: The correct canons of earlier kings were mixed with the delusive and false; discussions of great refinement were muddied with unrestrained extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The correct canons of earlier kings were mixed with the delusive and false; discussions of great refinement were muddied with unrestrained extravagance.

sentences.zh: 陵夷至於近代，去正轉疏，無複師資之法。

translations.literal: Decline reached recent times; departure from the correct grew ever more distant, and there was no longer any method of teacher and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Decline reached recent times; departure from the correct grew ever more distant, and there was no longer any method of teacher and precedent.

sentences.zh: 學不心解，專以浮華相尚，豫造雜難，擬為仇對，遂有芟角、反對、互從等諸翻競之說。

translations.literal: Study without understanding in the heart, exclusively honoring ornament and show; pre-fabricating mixed difficulties and posing them as adversarial pairs—thus there arose disputations of trimming corners, opposing sides, mutual following, and other competitive sophistries.
translations.idiomatic: Study without understanding in the heart, exclusively honoring ornament and show; pre-fabricating mixed difficulties and posing them as adversarial pairs—thus there arose disputations of trimming corners, opposing sides, mutual following, and other competitive sophistries.

sentences.zh: 馳騁煩言，以紊彝敘，嘵嘵成俗，而不知變，此學者之蔽也。

translations.literal: Galloping in verbose speech to disorder canonical order, clamor becoming custom without knowing change—this is the blindness of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Galloping in verbose speech to disorder canonical order, clamor becoming custom without knowing change—this is the blindness of scholars.

sentences.zh: 班固列六藝為九種，或以緯書解經，合為十種。

translations.literal: Ban Gu listed the Six Arts as nine categories, or with weft texts explaining the classics combined as ten categories.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu listed the Six Arts as nine categories, or with weft texts explaining the classics combined as ten categories.
